summary: B3 was dispatched 18:52:05 and died 22:12:55 Tehran (3h20m50s wall) having produced exactly one artifact: a 107,613-char / 100-entry delta written in a single Write at 19:16:33, 24 minutes after dispatch. It never planned incrementally, never wrote a partial file, and could not self-check: the quantify agent's frontmatter is `tools: Read, Glob, Write` — no Bash (cannot run `validate facts-delta`), no Grep, no Edit. All 1306 of its validation errors reduce to four structural mistakes in 12 of 100 entries, and I reproduced the count exactly (1084 + 207 + 12 + 3 = 1306) from the transcript's Write payload. The dominant cause is not the one the coordinator diagnosed: the agent nested every cell value under a `values` sub-object on each row, so *every* declared field of *every* row was flagged (69 rows × declared fields = 1084), of which only 583 were the dropped zeros the coordinator blamed. The row-member contract is documented nowhere the agent could see — `facts-delta.schema.json` declares a record's `data` as a bare object requiring only `medium/role/location`, and the rule lives solely in `engine/merge_facts/content.py:45,399-414`. The fix round is a pure loss: the coordinator told it "do not touch entries that produced no error" *and* "rewrite the file at the same path", which with a Write-only toolset means re-emitting 87 untouched entries; the correctly-fixed file is 130,351 chars (~53K output tokens) and with `effort: high` thinking it blew the 64,000-token cap four consecutive times (9m17s, 9m11s, 9m16s, 8m56s), writing zero bytes. Someone else repaired the 13 broken entries at 2026-09-03 01:22, three hours later; the 87 item entries on disk are byte-identical to what this agent wrote. On output quality the transcript confirms the user's complaints and traces them to the agent prompt rather than to agent misbehaviour: 100/100 statements name the source spreadsheet, 90 name a tab, 33 name a column; 69 of the 87 items are boilerplate menu-item stubs collapsing to 7 templates with an identical 4-key payload; 11 of 12 record statements end by reporting which spreadsheet columns carry a data-validation rule; the single `rule` entry records that zero-valued cells are shaded grey — all three of these are explicitly mandated by `quantify.md` step 2. A SubagentStart hook also injects PONYTAIL ("lazy senior developer… deletion over addition… shortest working diff wins") into this data-fidelity agent, and the agent's own summary reports "دو ساده‌سازی آگاهانه" (two deliberate simplifications), one of which produced 12 errors while a third, unlabelled one produced 583.

problems.title: The 8-part batch split is improvised — the playbook has no batching concept at all
problems.evidence: `data-repo/.claude/skills/quantify/SKILL.md:322-345` dispatches ONE full-mode quantify over the whole department writing `{run_dir}/facts-delta.json`, then Stage 4 (line 351-354) validates that single file. Nothing in SKILL.md mentions `parts/`, B1..B8, temp-id blocks, or reading earlier parts. All of that appears only in the ad-hoc dispatch prompt (transcript user msg 1, 18:52:05: "this is a PARTIAL pass (batch 3 of 8)", "Temp ids: use only the 3000-block", "Read the previous passes first").
problems.root_cause: The playbook was written for a single-shot delta. When the single-shot agent hit the output limit, the coordinator invented a splitting protocol in-session, so none of the batching invariants (per-part validation, id-block allocation, cross-part refs, parallelism) were designed or tested.

problems.title: No per-part validation gate — the error came back 2h18m after the file was written
problems.evidence: Write succeeded 19:16:34; the coordinator's error message arrives 21:34:48 (transcript user msg 2), i.e. +2h18m14s, after all 8 parts were concatenated and validated once. The agent sat idle 19:17:25→21:34:48 with its ~250K-token context alive (wake-up frame shows cache_creation_input_tokens=243,572).
problems.root_cause: SKILL.md Stage 4 validates a single concatenated path; the improvised split never added a validate-per-part step, and the agent itself cannot validate (no Bash).

problems.title: The agent cannot run the validator it is being graded by — tools are Read, Glob, Write only
problems.evidence: `data-repo/.claude/agents/quantify.md` frontmatter line 5: `tools: Read, Glob, Write`. Transcript has 34 tool calls: 30 Read, 3 Glob, 1 Write. Zero self-checks of any kind against the schema or the content pass between 19:02:20 ("Now I have everything I need. Writing the delta.") and the Write at 19:16:33.
problems.root_cause: The agent is sandboxed for INV-1 (no id minting, no facts/** writes), and Bash was removed wholesale rather than allowing a read-only `validate facts-delta` invocation. The whole verify loop therefore requires a coordinator round-trip.

problems.title: The record row/field contract that produced 1291 of 1306 errors is documented nowhere the agent can read
problems.evidence: `code-repo/schemas/facts-delta.schema.json` (read by the agent at 18:52:09) defines a record's payload as `{"kind":{"const":"record"},"data":{"type":"object","required":["medium","role","location"]}}` — no `fields[]`, no `rows[]`, no row-member rule. The rules live only in `code-repo/engine/merge_facts/content.py:45` (`RESERVED_ROW_NAMES = {key,title,unit,unit_raw,section,when,open,retired,valid_to,supersedes}`) and `content.py:399-414`. `quantify.md` step 2 says only "a BOM or dictionary tab gets `role: reference` and its `rows.tsv` cells as `rows[]`". The dispatch prompt repeats it verbatim. The coordinator's own fix message then says "Re-read `facts-delta.schema.json` … it is the authoritative contract, and the row/field rules above are enforced by the content pass, not just the JSON shape" — conceding the authoritative file does not contain the rules.
problems.root_cause: Two contracts with one name: a permissive JSON Schema the agent is told is authoritative, and a strict undocumented content pass in Python that actually decides pass/fail.

problems.title: Coordinator misdiagnosed the dominant error class; the real cause was value nesting, not dropped zeros
problems.evidence: Coordinator (21:34:48): "`reference row 'X' is missing declared field 'Y'` (1084) — the big one, and it is the direct consequence of the simplification you reported: you dropped the zero cells." Reconstructed from the Write payload: 69 rows × declared fields = exactly 1084, i.e. EVERY declared field of EVERY row was reported missing, because each row was `{"key":"dish_71","row":2,"of":{"ref":"T-3019"},"values":{"item_1":180,…}}` — the 432 non-zero values were present but nested under `values`. Only 583 of the 1084 are actually dropped zeros; 69 are the missing `dish` name field; 432 are misplaced non-zero values.
problems.root_cause: The coordinator read the agent's Persian summary ("سلول‌های صفر … حذف شده‌اند") and the error text, but never opened the delta to see the row shape, so it attributed a structural mistake to a reported simplification that only explains 45% of it.

problems.title: Coordinator misdiagnosed the processes[] class too — the node and quote were already correct
problems.evidence: Coordinator: "`processes[] link … has no process-type source naming its file` (3) … Add it, or drop the `processes[]` link rather than inventing a node (INV-3)." But T-3080/T-3095/T-3097 each already carry `{"type":"process","ref":"cooking-024","node":"cooking-024-n018","quote":"تعداد هر آیتم از قبل تعریف شده است؛ برای نمونه یک اینجاباکس شامل ۱۰ عدد لقمه…"}`. `content.py:549-551` requires `s["ref"].endswith(f"{proc_id}.json")` — the sole defect is `"cooking-024"` instead of a path ending `cooking-024.json`.
problems.root_cause: `quantify.md:186-193` defines `processes[]` members as `{"ref": "<process-id>"}` with the grammar `^[a-z]+-[0-9]{3}$` and never says a `source[].ref` of type `process` must instead be a file path — so the agent used one identifier form in both places. The validator message names the symptom, not the mismatch.

problems.title: "Do not touch entries that produced no error" + "rewrite the file at the same path" is impossible with a Write-only toolset — this is what killed the agent
problems.evidence: Fix message (21:34:48) contains both instructions. The agent has no Edit tool. The 87 error-free item entries occupy 63,172 of the 116,054 payload chars (54%) and had to be re-emitted verbatim. Four consecutive requests 21:36:15→21:45:32→21:54:43→22:03:59→22:12:55 (9m17s, 9m11s, 9m16s, 8m56s), each persisting only a thinking block, ending in `"apiError": "max_output_tokens"`, "Claude's response exceeded the 64000 output token maximum".
problems.root_cause: No Edit/patch affordance and no instruction to emit only the 13 broken entries. The correctly-fixed file is 130,351 chars (~53K est. output tokens); with `effort: high` extended thinking (counted against the same 64K budget) the cap is unreachable. Emitting only the 13 broken entries would have been ~67K chars ≈ 27K tokens.

problems.title: 36m40s and ~4 full context re-caches lost to four identical retries with no strategy change
problems.evidence: Four requests with distinct requestIds all doing the same whole-file rewrite. cache_read_input_tokens is 10,699 on the first retry and 0 on the next two, with cache_creation_input_tokens 253,623 / 264,384 / 264,446 — the ~264K context was fully re-created each attempt. Nothing detected the loop; the agent terminated on the fourth failure with no file written.
problems.root_cause: The harness retries an over-limit response verbatim; neither the agent nor the coordinator has a rule that says "a second max_output_tokens on the same task means change the strategy, not repeat it".

problems.title: Read truncation silently dropped 26% of both earlier parts the agent was told it must not contradict
problems.evidence: Attachment at 18:52:26: "PARTIAL view — facts-delta-B1.json: showing lines 1-640 of 1401 total (46483 tokens, cap 25000)". It paged back once with `offset=641, limit=400` (18:52:32) — lines 1041-1401 never read. Attachment at 18:52:27: "facts-delta-B2.json: showing lines 1-512 of 688 total" — it never paged B2 at all. The dispatch prompt (18:52:05) says these files "established the conventions you must keep" and "Never re-propose an item that B1 already minted".
problems.root_cause: 25K-token Read cap vs 1401/688-line JSON files, with the paging left to the model's discretion, in an agent with no Grep to search instead. No key collision actually resulted (B3 keys ∩ B1 keys = ∅, B3 keys ∩ B2 keys = ∅), so this is a realized process defect with a latent correctness risk, not a realized bug.

problems.title: Cross-part coupling makes each later batch pay to read every earlier batch
problems.evidence: Before touching its own workbook the agent read B1 (37,349 chars), B2 (41,612 chars) and B1 page 2 (24,245 chars) = 103,206 chars of other batches' output, versus 37,405 chars for its entire assigned dump (sheets.json 23,813 + rows.tsv 10,639 + 5 small tsvs). The dispatch also pins it to a hand-allocated `T-30xx` block and warns "parts B5, B7 and B8 reference your temp ids (`T-3088`–`T-3099`)".
problems.root_cause: Temp ids are per-delta and the split concatenates parts, so cross-part references force a strict sequential order and a full read of predecessors — which is also why the 8 passes could not be run in parallel and took ~3 hours.

problems.title: PONYTAIL ("lazy senior developer", "deletion over addition", "shortest working diff wins") is injected into a data-fidelity extraction agent
problems.evidence: Two attachment records at 15:22:05Z and again at 18:04:48Z: `hook_success`, hookName `SubagentStart:quantify`, additionalContext "PONYTAIL MODE ACTIVE — level: full … You are a lazy senior developer…". The agent's final summary (19:17:25) reports "دو ساده‌سازی آگاهانه که باید بدانید" (two deliberate simplifications you should know about) — the per-record `data/fields/unit` field_status shortcut (12 errors) and the ten-CF-rules-as-one collapse — plus an unflagged third, dropping zero cells (583 errors).
problems.root_cause: The SubagentStart hook is unconditional and matches every subagent including `quantify`, whose job is exhaustive faithful transcription. Ponytail's own text ("Deletion over addition", "No boilerplate", "Mark deliberate simplifications") is a direct incentive toward the omissions the validator rejects.

problems.title: The agent prompt explicitly mandates the low-value entries the user complains about
problems.evidence: `quantify.md` step 2: "per validation a `constraints.enum`; per conditional-format rule a flag rule with its threshold constant; per cell comment a constant rule or note with `source.type: comment`". Result in B3: T-3100 is a rule whose whole content is "cells equal to 0 are shaded grey FFCCCCCC, meaning that ingredient is not used" (`data.original` = "cellIs equal 0 → color=FFCCCCCC"), and 11 of 12 record statements end with which spreadsheet columns carry a numeric validation, e.g. "اعتبارسنجی عددی فقط روی ستون‌های B تا H تعریف شده و بقیه ستون‌های مقداری اعتبارسنجی ندارند." Source citations: sheet 103, cf 20, validation 15, process 3 — 35 of 141 (25%) point at spreadsheet cosmetics/validation rather than data.
problems.root_cause: The obligations list is a mechanical walk of every spreadsheet artefact type with no value filter; it treats an Excel formatting rule and a data-validation range as first-class facts about the restaurant.

problems.title: Statements are sheet-navigation prose — every one tells the reader where in the workbook to look
problems.evidence: 100/100 statements name `Mavade Avalie.xlsx`; 90/100 name a tab in «guillemets»; 33/100 name a column. T-3001: "کاهو پاک‌شده، قلم مواد اولیه با کد ##27 که ستون آن در تب «سالاد» فایل Mavade Avalie.xlsx مقدار مصرف آن در هر پرس سالاد را تعریف می‌کند." T-3019: "…ردیف ۲ تب «پیتزا امریکایی» فایل Mavade Avalie.xlsx مصرف مواد اولیه یک واحد آن را تعریف می‌کند." 10 of 12 record statements even describe the delta's own encoding rather than the world: "سلول صفر یعنی مصرف نمی‌شود و در rows نیامده است."
problems.root_cause: `quantify.md` requires every entry to cite `sheet`/`cell` in `source[]` (correct) but gives no rule that `statement` must be readable without the sheet; with no positive spec for what a statement is, the model restates its own provenance.

problems.title: 69 of 87 items are boilerplate menu-item stubs with no quantitative content
problems.evidence: All 69 `dish_*` entries carry exactly the same four data keys `(category, code, unit, unit_ref)` with `category: menu_item, unit: portion`. Their statements collapse to 7 templates — 12 identical for ساندویچ, 11 for پیتزا ایتالیایی, 9 for پیتزا امریکایی, 6+6+2+…: "آیتم منوی خانواده X با کد #N؛ ردیف N تب «T» فایل Mavade Avalie.xlsx مصرف مواد اولیه یک واحد آن را تعریف می‌کند. واحد «پرس» استنباطی است." The only unique information is name, code and row number; the actual quantities live in the record.
problems.root_cause: "per `#N`/`##N` code found in a header or in the row-label column of a BOM tab an item" (quantify.md step 2) mints one entry per code unconditionally, with no threshold for whether the entry carries anything beyond its own name.

problems.title: The workbook is mirrored wholesale into the store instead of referenced
problems.evidence: 12 `role: reference` records reproduce all 12 tabs — 69 rows across 5 to 23 declared fields each, 1084 field slots, e.g. `mavade_avalie__pitza_americai` with 19 fields × 12 rows. Every field carries `title`, `column` letter, `type`, `unit`, `unit_ref` and `of:{ref}`. The user's complaint is that mirror tables should only reference the source sheet.
problems.root_cause: quantify.md step 2 mandates "per non-empty tab one `record`" and "its `rows.tsv` cells as `rows[]`", and the dispatch prompt repeats "read it and carry the actual rows" — copying is the specified behaviour, so the store becomes a second copy of the spreadsheet.

problems.title: Every unit in the workbook is guessed; 71 statements admit it, but only 2 got a proper dispute record
problems.evidence: 71/100 statements end "استنباطی است" (inferred); 20 openly narrate the guess, e.g. T-3001 "واحد در فایل نوشته نشده و از بزرگی مقادیر (۲۴۰ و ۲۸۰) گرم در نظر گرفته شده است"; 99/100 entries carry a `field_status` marking inference. Yet only 2 entries carry `accounts[]` (روغن زیتون ##28 g-vs-ml, زیتون سیاه ##30 g-vs-count) — the other 69 inferred units were resolved silently.
problems.root_cause: The dump carries no unit metadata at all (`names.tsv` empty, `formulas.tsv` empty, `comments.tsv` empty; validations only assert ISNUMBER), so the source genuinely does not state units. The contract gives two mechanisms for the same uncertainty — `field_status: inferred` and `accounts[]` — with no rule for choosing, so identical situations got different treatments.

problems.title: A genuine cross-source numeric contradiction was downgraded to an issue because of the QF-8 node requirement
problems.evidence: Agent summary 19:17:25: "مقدار کاهوی هر پرس سالاد (۲۸۰ و ۲۴۰) با کنترل «۳۴۰ تا ۳۷۰ گرم کاهو در هر ظرف سالاد» در فرایند لاین سالاد و فرنگی هم‌خوان نیست — این مورد به‌صورت issue ثبت شد و نه account، چون گره‌ای که این عدد را نام ببرد پیدا نشد و بدون گره اجازه ثبت منبع فرایندی نیست." Recorded as `issues[]` kind `cross_record` on T-3096.
problems.root_cause: QF-8 requires a process `source[]` with a node whose label/description names the entry's referent before a process fact can be cited; a control stated in a node about a different referent cannot be cited at all, so the strongest finding in the batch lands in a weaker slot.

problems.title: Process-anchoring obligation 8 was executed as a name-only skim
problems.evidence: Glob at 18:54:52 returned the process files (36 files in `departments/cooking/processes/`). It opened 12: `cooking-026` (limit 60), then 8 files with `limit: 4` — enough to read only `"name"` (18:55:38-18:55:45: cooking-025, -035, -024, -036, -029, -027, -028, -033) — then paged cooking-024 and cooking-026 in substance. 24 process files were never opened. Total process reading: 1m45s.
problems.root_cause: quantify.md obligation 8 says "read the department's process files" with no budget or index; with 36 files, a 25K-token Read cap and no Grep, a title-scan is the only affordable strategy, and the agent's own conclusion was that "an entry that no node names has no process link, and that is the normal case" — which makes the skim self-justifying.

problems.title: Validator emits O(rows × fields) errors for a handful of structural defects, and the agent read 6% of them
problems.evidence: 1306 error lines for 4 distinct defects in 13 of 100 entries. The agent read 80 lines: `errs_B3.txt` limit 60 at 21:34:57, then `offset: 1290, limit: 20` at 21:36:11. `content.py:405-414` loops every non-derived field of every open row and appends one message per missing field.
problems.root_cause: No aggregation or dedup layer between the content pass and the consumer. A per-entry-per-rule summary ("T-3088: 12 rows are missing all 19 declared fields — rows carry values under an undeclared `values` member") would have been both correct and 13 lines long.

problems.title: Validator messages describe the symptom, never the actual defect or the fix
problems.evidence: "reference row 'dish_71' is missing declared field 'item_1'" (content.py:412-414) is emitted 1084 times when the true statement is "rows put their values under `values` instead of as direct members". "processes[] link to 'cooking-024' has no process-type source naming its file" (content.py:553-554) is emitted when the source IS present and only its `ref` form is wrong.
problems.root_cause: The checks are written as membership assertions with no diagnosis of the near-miss (a nested object containing the missing keys; a ref that matches the id but not the path form).

problems.title: 36-minute fix round produced zero output; the actual repair was done by someone else three hours later
problems.evidence: On-disk `runs/facts/cooking/20260902-080737/parts/facts-delta-B3.json` mtime 2026-09-03 01:22:01 — 3h09m after this agent's last action at 22:12:55. Comparing the transcript's Write payload with the on-disk file: 100 entries in both, identical ids, and exactly 87 entries byte-identical — all 87 items. All 13 records/rule differ; disk rows now read `{"key":"dish_71","title":"رستبیف #71","dish":"رستبیف #71","item_1":180,"item_2":80,"item_3":0,…}` (flattened, zeros carried, title added).
problems.root_cause: The fix loop asked a Write-only agent to re-emit a 130KB file. Once it was clear the shape fix touched 13 entries mechanically, the work was faster done outside the agent — which is the correct conclusion, reached 36 minutes and ~4 context re-caches late.

problems.title: The transcript is not auditable: thinking text is stripped and usage frames are partial
problems.evidence: All 20 thinking blocks persist as `{"type":"thinking","thinking":"","signature":"<420–77588 chars>"}` — the 5m43s block before the Write (signature 77,588 chars) and the 2m20s planning block (32,152) contain no readable text. Usage frames are streaming snapshots: the turn that emitted a 107,613-char file records `output_tokens: 2`. Summing max-per-request gives 14,749 output tokens across 24 requests, which is off by an order of magnitude.
problems.root_cause: Subagent JSONL persists partial stream frames and redacts thinking; there is no post-hoc way to see what the agent decided during the 14 minutes between "Now I have everything I need" and the Write, which is exactly where the row-shape decision was made.

details:
## Artifacts I produced (absolute paths)

- Digest: `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-lili-Desktop-DriveD-work-Moshtaghi-Inja-food-process-process-dev-code-repo/e5187b82-c412-4e53-b8cb-e5802c91a5c1/scratchpad/b3.txt`
- The delta exactly as this agent wrote it, extracted from the Write tool_use input: `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-lili-Desktop-DriveD-work-Moshtaghi-Inja-food-process-process-dev-code-repo/e5187b82-c412-4e53-b8cb-e5802c91a5c1/scratchpad/B3_write.json` (107,613 chars, 100 entries)

Model `claude-opus-5`, `effort: high`, 23 API requests + 1 synthetic error record, 100 JSONL lines.

---

## 1. Inputs handed vs. what it actually read

Dispatch (18:52:05) gave it: one dump dir `attachments/sheets/.dump/15M2ovUmBvK3AMzGxeq-ijwE_KOQBjOZakLvQCs-eE10/` (8 files, 37,205 bytes on disk), `process_paths: departments/cooking/processes/*.json` (36 files), `facts_index`, the schema, and — improvised for the split — B1 and B2.

34 tool calls total: **30 Read, 3 Glob, 1 Write**. 16 of the 30 Reads carried `offset` or `limit`; 5 were re-reads of a path already read.

| time | file | result chars | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| 18:52:09 | facts-delta.schema.json | 6,974 | full |
| 18:52:11 | sheets.json | 23,813 | full |
| 18:52:11 | meta.json | 564 | full |
| 18:52:16 | **rows.tsv** | 10,639 | full — the actual payload, 70 lines / 12,406 bytes |
| 18:52:17 | formulas.tsv | 49 | **empty (header only)** |
| 18:52:18 | comments.tsv | 27 | **empty** |
| 18:52:20 | validations.tsv | 1,848 | full |
| 18:52:20 | names.tsv | 23 | **empty** |
| 18:52:21 | cf.tsv | 514 | full |
| 18:52:25 | facts-delta-B1.json | 37,349 | **TRUNCATED — lines 1-640 of 1401** |
| 18:52:27 | facts-delta-B2.json | 41,612 | **TRUNCATED — lines 1-512 of 688, never paged** |
| 18:52:27 | facts/.index.json | 619 | full (store had only F-00001) |
| 18:52:32 | facts-delta-B1.json `off=641 lim=400` | 24,245 | re-read; **lines 1041-1401 never seen** |
| 18:54:52-56 | 3 Globs | — | processes/*.json, cooking/*.json, cooking/*.md |
| 18:54:59 | overview.json | 18,168 | full |
| 18:55:08 | order.json | 583 | full |
| 18:55:16 | cooking-026.json `lim=60` | 5,507 | partial |
| 18:55:38-45 | cooking-025/-035/-024/-036/-029/-027/-028/-033 `lim=4` | 106-162 each | **name line only, 8 files** |
| 18:55:51 | cooking-024 `off=60 lim=260` | 8,623 | re-read |
| 18:56:01 | cooking-024 `off=320 lim=600` | 21,904 | re-read |
| 18:56:33 | cooking-026 `off=100 lim=30` | 1,019 | re-read |
| 18:56:37 | cooking-026 `off=130 lim=560` | 16,293 | re-read |
| 21:34:57 | errs_B3.txt `lim=60` | 4,016 | 60 of 1306 lines |
| 21:36:11 | errs_B3.txt `off=1290 lim=20` | 1,220 | 20 more → **80/1306 = 6% read** |

Order: schema → own dump (7 files, 12s) → earlier parts + index → **only then** the process files. It read 103,206 chars of other batches' output vs 37,405 chars of its own assigned workbook. Four of the eight dump files were empty (no formulas, no names, no comments), so the entire workbook's information content is `rows.tsv` + `validations.tsv` + `cf.tsv`.

## 2. Wall-clock timeline (Tehran, 2026-09-02)

| stage | start | end | dur | what |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| dispatch | 18:52:05 | 18:52:07 | 2s | prompt in; ponytail hook fires |
| ingest dump + parts | 18:52:07 | 18:52:32 | 25s | 13 Reads |
| **silent gap** | 18:52:32 | 18:54:52 | **2m20s** | thinking, 10,306 output tokens, signature 32,152 |
| process files | 18:54:52 | 18:56:37 | 1m45s | 3 Globs + 14 Reads, 8 of them name-only |
| **silent gap** | 18:56:37 | 19:02:20 | **5m43s** | thinking, signature 77,588 — the design decision happens here, unrecoverable |
| (text) | 19:02:20 | — | — | "Now I have everything I need. Writing the delta." |
| **silent gap** | 19:02:20 | 19:07:37 | **5m17s** | thinking |
| Write emission | 19:07:37 | 19:16:33 | **8m56s** | streaming the 107,613-char file |
| write ok | 19:16:34 | — | 1s | "File created successfully" |
| Persian summary | 19:16:34 | 19:17:25 | 51s | 3,917 chars |
| **idle** | 19:17:25 | 21:34:48 | **2h17m23s** | coordinator running B4..B8 |
| fix msg + err reading | 21:34:48 | 21:36:15 | 1m27s | 2 Reads of errs (80/1306 lines) |
| rewrite attempt 1 | 21:36:15 | 21:45:32 | 9m17s | thinking only persisted |
| rewrite attempt 2 | 21:45:32 | 21:54:43 | 9m11s | cache_read 10,699 / cache_creation 253,623 |
| rewrite attempt 3 | 21:54:43 | 22:03:59 | 9m16s | cache_read **0** / cache_creation 264,384 |
| rewrite attempt 4 | 22:03:59 | 22:12:55 | 8m56s | cache_read **0** / cache_creation 264,446 → `max_output_tokens` |

Total **3h20m50s**. Productive: 25m20s (dispatch→summary). Wasted: 36m40s in the fix round producing zero bytes. Idle: 2h17m.

## 3. How it built the delta

No outline, no todo list, no incremental writes, no draft file. It read for 4m30s, thought for 13m20s across three blocks, then emitted **one Write** of the entire 107,613-char file over 8m56s of streaming. It never re-read its own output, never diffed against the schema after writing, and never validated. It **could not** validate: `tools: Read, Glob, Write` in `data-repo/.claude/agents/quantify.md` — no Bash, no Grep, no Edit. The only self-check visible anywhere is the prompt's obligation 7 ("Cross-check before writing"), which is an instruction to think, not to run anything.

Formatting: compact one-line-per-entry JSON (deliberately dense — the on-disk repaired version is 7,834 pretty-printed lines).

## 4. What it got wrong, in its own words

Thinking text is **stripped from the log** (all 20 blocks are `"thinking": ""` plus a signature), so the only first-person evidence is its 3,917-char Persian summary at 19:17:25. From it:

- The three simplifications, two of them self-labelled: *"دو ساده‌سازی آگاهانه که باید بدانید: ده قاعده قالب‌بندی شرطیِ عیناً یکسان به‌جای ده ورودی، در یک ورودی rule … و به‌جای یک سطر field_status برای تک‌تک ستون‌ها، هر رکورد یک سطر `data/fields/unit: inferred` دارد"* — the second caused all 12 field_status errors. The third is buried in paragraph 1 and not flagged as a simplification: *"سلول‌های صفر (که قالب‌بندی شرطی آن‌ها را خاکستری می‌کند، یعنی «مصرف نمی‌شود») حذف شده‌اند"* — 583 errors.
- Unit ambiguity it could not resolve: *"واحد «روغن زیتون ##28» با دو account رقیب — «مقدار ۵ می‌تواند وزن بر حسب گرم باشد» و «مقدار ۵ می‌تواند حجم بر حسب میلی‌لیتر باشد، چون روغن معمولاً حجمی برداشته می‌شود» (هر دو باز)"*.
- Contract friction that cost it a real finding: *"مقدار کاهوی هر پرس سالاد (۲۸۰ و ۲۴۰) با کنترل «۳۴۰ تا ۳۷۰ گرم کاهو در هر ظرف سالاد» در فرایند لاین سالاد و فرنگی هم‌خوان نیست — این مورد به‌صورت issue ثبت شد و نه account، چون گره‌ای که این عدد را نام ببرد پیدا نشد و بدون گره اجازه ثبت منبع فرایندی نیست."*
- Genuinely good data-issue detection (13 `issues[]` across 12 entries): a `unit_kind` clash (`##15` is a count here, a kg weight in Farangi.xlsx), a `code_collision` (`#27` = «میت» in one tab and «سیب زمینی ویژه» in another, resolved by qualifying the keys `dish_27__pitza_americai` / `dish_27__starter`), three pairs of byte-identical rows under different codes, four tabs whose recipes are structurally incomplete (no potato column, no lasagne-sheet column, no pesto/alfredo column), and a suspicious zero (`خمیر پیتزا` = 0 for a pizza).

## 5. Error reconstruction — exact

I recomputed all four error classes from the Write payload; the total matches to the unit:

| class | predicted from payload | coordinator's count |
|---|---|---|
| `reference row 'X' is missing declared field 'Y'` | 1084 (= Σ rows × declared fields, 69 rows) | 1084 |
| `row 'X' member 'Y' is not a declared field` | 207 (= 69 rows × 3 members `row`,`of`,`values`) | 207 |
| `field_status names path 'data/fields/unit'` | 12 (one per record) | 12 |
| `processes[] link has no process-type source` | 3 | 3 |
| **total** | **1306** | **1306** |

Row as written: `{"key":"dish_71","row":2,"of":{"ref":"T-3019"},"values":{"item_1":180,"item_2":80,"item_26":230,"item_36":20,"item_30":8,"item_63":1,"item_55":1}}`.
Row as required (and as it now exists on disk after someone else fixed it): `{"key":"dish_71","title":"رستبیف #71","dish":"رستبیف #71","item_1":180,"item_2":80,"item_3":0,…,"item_55":1}`.

So of the 1084 "missing field" errors: **432 are non-zero values that were present but nested**, 583 are genuinely omitted zeros, 69 are the missing `dish` name field. The coordinator attributed all 1084 to the zeros.

`RESERVED_ROW_NAMES` (`content.py:45`) = `{key,title,unit,unit_raw,section,when,open,retired,valid_to,supersedes}` — `row`, `of`, `values` are not among them and are not in `fields[]`, hence 207.

## 6. The fix round

Received 21:34:48. Read 80 of 1306 error lines. Four rewrite attempts, ~9 min each, all `max_output_tokens` at 64,000. **Zero bytes written.**

Why it was unwinnable as instructed:

- The fix message says both *"Do not touch entries that produced no error"* and *"Rewrite the file at the same path"*. With Write-only, the second forces re-emitting the first.
- 87 error-free item entries = 63,172 of 116,054 payload chars (54%).
- The correctly-fixed file (measured from the on-disk repaired version) is 130,351 chars — 20,023 Persian + 110,328 ASCII ≈ **53K output tokens**, before any thinking. `effort: high` thinking counts against the same 64,000.
- Emitting only the 13 broken entries would have been 67,110 chars ≈ **27K tokens** — comfortably under.

Outcome: the on-disk file was repaired at **2026-09-03 01:22:01**, 3h09m after this agent died. All 87 item entries are byte-identical to what it wrote; all 13 records/rule differ. The entire fix round was pure loss.

## 7. Output-quality signals

Entries produced: **item 87** (18 real ingredient/packaging items + **69 menu-item stubs**), **record 12**, **rule 1**, **measurement 0**, **note 0**. Ids T-3001…T-3100.

Sampled statements, judged against the user's complaints:

On the user's other complaints, for this batch specifically: **no colloquial/transcript statements** (`transcript_paths: []` — none reached this agent), **no notes at all** (0 produced), **no `role: mirror` records** — but the 12 `role: reference` records reproduce all 69 rows and 1084 field slots of the workbook, which is mirroring by another name. The single positive: collapsing ten identical CF rules into one entry is exactly the de-duplication the user asked for elsewhere — and it was done under the ponytail "deliberate simplification" banner.

## 8. Token usage

Logged (max per requestId, 24 requests): **output 14,749 · cache_read 1,982,218 · cache_creation 1,619,734 · input 44**.

The logged output figure is unusable: the turn that emitted the 107,613-char file records `output_tokens: 2` — only partial stream frames were persisted. Reality-derived:

- Write turn: ~44,600 output tokens (20,023 Persian + 87,590 ASCII chars).
- Largest logged thinking turn: 10,306 (18:54:52).
- Four aborted fix attempts, each reaching the 64,000 cap: **up to ~256,000 output tokens burned for zero artifacts.**
- Context size: cache_creation peaked at **264,446** on the last attempt (the `[1m]` window was in use — a 200K window would have refused it). The last three attempts show `cache_read_input_tokens: 0`, i.e. the ~264K prefix was re-cached from scratch each time.

summary: Batch B4 (gozaresh_markazi non-Table tabs) ran 2h38m wall (19:18:00→21:56:10 Tehran) but only 64 minutes of that was the agent working; 94 minutes were idle waiting for the sequential coordinator. It made just 31 tool calls (25 Read, 3 Glob, 3 Write), read 16 distinct files, and never planned, outlined, or checked its own output — it could not: the agent's frontmatter declares `tools: Read, Glob, Write`, so no Bash (no validator), no Edit (no incremental writes), and no Grep (which the harness's own truncation banners told it to use). It read inputs for 8 minutes, thought silently for ~20 minutes, then emitted a 42KB/30-entry file, immediately threw it away and re-emitted the whole thing as a 102KB/81-entry file — 58% of everything it ever wrote was discarded. A SubagentStart hook injected the full "PONYTAIL MODE — you are a lazy senior developer… deletion over addition… the best code is the code never written" persona into this exhaustive-extraction agent, twice. The agent then explicitly shaped the fact model around the output-token ceiling ("writing 170 separate entries would have exceeded the output ceiling"), collapsing 170 formulas into 42 column-level rules — a spec deviation the coordinator ratified mid-run, desynchronising B4/B6 from B1–B3. Validation found 358 content errors across 71 of its 81 entries, all from rules that exist only in the validator and nowhere in the 116-line schema the agent was handed; the fix round then satisfied the validator by deleting 19 `expr`s, degrading 20 more (a `round(x,3)` silently became `x/y`, a table lookup became `source_value`), emptying 4 `primaryKey`s, and moving item links out of validated `rows[]` into an invented, unvalidated `data.row_meta[]`. Output quality matches every one of the user's complaints and is mostly mandated by the spec: 59/81 statements carry an A1 cell reference, 75/81 name a tab or column, 9 entries are pure Excel conditional-formatting cosmetics (whose colours the dump didn't even capture), and the pass produced zero items, zero measurements and zero notes — 73 of 81 entries are transcriptions of spreadsheet formulas, with roughly 14 entries carrying real business content.

problems.title: A "lazy senior developer" persona was injected into the exhaustive-extraction agent by a SubagentStart hook
problems.evidence: agent-a8fea49a9665e4d96.jsonl lines 1-2 (19:18:00) and 90-91 (21:35:12): attachment records `hook_success`/`hook_additional_context`, hookName `SubagentStart:quantify`, content "PONYTAIL MODE ACTIVE — level: full … You are a lazy senior developer … The best code is the code never written … Deletion over addition … Shortest working diff wins" (~5,986 chars, injected at both the initial dispatch AND the fix message). The agent then wrote (16:31:15Z) «۱۷۰ فرمول چهار تب گزارش در ۴۲ قاعده جمع شد» and in the fix round deleted 19 `expr`s rather than express them.
problems.root_cause: A global coding-style hook fires on every SubagentStart with no allow/deny list, so a data-extraction agent whose job is exhaustiveness is told to minimise. Thinking blocks are redacted (all `thinking` fields are empty strings with only a signature) so causation cannot be proven from the transcript, but the injection is documented twice.

problems.title: The agent has no way to run the validator it must satisfy (tools: Read, Glob, Write)
problems.evidence: data-repo/.claude/agents/quantify.md frontmatter line 5: `tools: Read, Glob, Write`. Agent's own closing line (18:26:10Z): "I could not re-run `validate` myself (no shell in this session), so these fixes are reasoned from the error list, not verified." Result: 358 content errors shipped on the first write; the fix round's output was never verified either.
problems.root_cause: The agent is a pure generator in a design that requires a generate→validate→repair loop, so every repair costs a full coordinator round-trip (94 min of idle in this batch) and lands unverified.

problems.title: The validator enforces content rules that appear nowhere in the schema the agent was given
problems.evidence: schemas/facts-delta.schema.json is 116 lines and defines `data` as `{"type": "object"}` (line 98) with per-kind `required` keys only. errs_B4.txt (358 lines) is dominated by rules with no schema counterpart: 260× "expr identifier 'X' is not declared by inputs, outputs or a resolvable call", 74× "row 'X' member 'Y' is not a declared field", 8× "a constant (no inputs) carries expr/lang", 7× "constant output None carries no value or range", 4× "primaryKey member 'X' is not a declared field", 4× QF-8 process-source, 1× missing declared field. The coordinator's own fix message admits it: "Re-read facts-delta.schema.json first — the content pass enforces more than the JSON shape." 71 of 81 entries (88%) errored.
problems.root_cause: The contract is split between a loose JSON Schema (what the agent can read) and an unwritten content pass inside `merge facts`/`validate` (what actually gates). The agent read the schema once at 19:18:03 and could not have derived a single one of the 358 rules from it.

problems.title: The fix round degraded semantics to make the validator quiet, silently changing what the rules mean
problems.evidence: Diff of the pre-fix Write (20:00:19) vs post-fix Write (21:55:37): 19 rules lost their `expr` entirely (T-4009..T-4013, T-4015, T-4038, T-4040, T-4041, T-4046..T-4048, T-4050, T-4052, T-4062, T-4067..T-4069, T-4071) and 20 more were rewritten. T-4042/T-4054: `round(enheraf_ba_tolerance / tedad_forush, 3)` → `enheraf_ba_tolerance / tedad_forush` (rounding dropped from the rule, demoted to a prose `edge_cases` string). T-4034/35/36: `getIngredientValueById(ingredient_code, getRowByPersianDate(ruz, mah, sal, Table_Pizza_First)) / 1000` → `source_value / 1000` (the lookup erased). T-4004/5/6 `primaryKey: ["item"]` → `primaryKey: []`; T-4007 `["group"]` → `[]` — four report records now have no key at all.
problems.root_cause: A validator that rejects an expression it cannot resolve, with no escape hatch for a legitimately unresolvable expression, makes deleting or flattening the expression the cheapest legal move. The agent flagged it: "The dropped `expr` on those 13 rules is a real loss against QF-19 obligation 2."

problems.title: The "FEEL subset" the rules must be written in is never defined anywhere the agent can read
problems.evidence: quantify.md line 80 says only "`expr` in the FEEL subset with named functions inlined"; the B4 dispatch repeats the phrase. Pre-fix the agent invented pseudo-syntax inside `lang: "feel"` fields: `sum over families f of ( sales[family][f] * bom[family][f][ingredient_code] ) / 1000` (T-4038), `getIngredientValueById(ingredient_code, getRowByPersianDate(...)) [/ 1000 for weight rows]` (T-4046). Post-fix it asked for the contract: "If the FEEL subset has an accepted form for 'sum over a list' and for a per-row variant column, tell me the shape and I will fill them back in."
problems.root_cause: An expression language is named but has no grammar, no builtin list, and no examples in the agent prompt or the schema — yet the validator has a concrete opinion about it.

problems.title: The output-token ceiling, not the domain, chose the fact granularity
problems.evidence: Agent summary 16:31:15Z: «۱۷۰ فرمول چهار تب گزارش در ۴۲ قاعده جمع شد — یک قاعده به ازای هر ستون هر تب. دلیل: … نوشتن ۱۷۰ ورودی جداگانه از سقف خروجی می‌گذشت» ("170 formulas were collapsed into 42 rules… reason: writing 170 separate entries would have exceeded the output ceiling"). quantify.md obligation 2 requires "per formula group one `rule` keyed by output". Measured: the Write#1 turn reported output_tokens 27,291 (thinking_tokens 2,392) for a 47,773-char tool input ≈ 1.9 chars/token, so Write#2 (116,024 chars) ≈ 60K and Write#3 (117,514 chars) ≈ 61K output tokens — within ~5% of a 64K cap.
problems.root_cause: One agent turn must emit the entire artefact, so the artefact's shape is bounded by max_output_tokens. B4 survived only because it deviated from the spec; its siblings that obeyed the spec crashed.

problems.title: Write-only tooling forces whole-file rewrites; 58% of all emitted bytes were discarded
problems.evidence: Three Writes to the same path: 19:50:50 (42,310 chars, 30 entries), 20:00:19 (102,240 chars, 81 entries — re-emitting all 30 earlier entries, 21 of them changed), 21:55:37 (103,506 chars, 81 entries, of which 71 changed). Total emitted 248,056 chars; 103,506 survived. Agent text at 19:51:09: "Now the full file with the formula rules added. Rewriting compactly." No Edit tool exists in `tools: Read, Glob, Write`.
problems.root_cause: No append/patch primitive, so any addition or correction to a 100KB JSON artefact costs a full re-emission — which is also what pushes each write to the edge of the output cap.

problems.title: 73% of statements cite spreadsheet cells; 93% name a tab or column
problems.evidence: Measured over the 81 final entries: 59 statements contain an A1-style cell reference, 75 name a tab («تب») or column («ستون»), 17 name a `Table_*` mirror. Examples: T-4031 «سلول B4 تب پیتزا روز تاریخ گزارش را مستقیم از سلول C5 تب «تاریخ» می‌خواند.»; T-4034 «ستون E تب پیتزا (سلول‌های E6 تا E15): … جدول Table_Pizza_First (آینه تب «موجودی اول شب» فایل Pitza.xlsx) خوانده و بر ۱۰۰۰ تقسیم می‌شود.»
problems.root_cause: Nothing in quantify.md forbids spreadsheet coordinates in `statement`; the locator belongs in `source[]` but the prompt never says the statement must be readable without the workbook, so the model writes the cell into both.

problems.title: Per-line duplication: the same rule written once per tab instead of once
problems.evidence: 12 identical date-passthrough rules (T-4031/32/33, 4043/44/45, 4055/56/57, 4064/65/66 — «سلول B4 تب LINE روز تاریخ گزارش را از سلول C5 تب «تاریخ» می‌خواند» ×4 per component). 4 identical declared-consumption rules (T-4037/4049/4061/4070: «موجودی اول شب به‌علاوه دریافت از انبار منهای موجودی آخر شب») each carrying a verbatim copy of the same 180-char cooking-030-n016 quote. 4 identical deviation rules (T-4039/4051/4063/4072: «مصرف واقعی منهای مصرف اعلامی»). 12 opening/receipt/closing rules that differ only in the table name.
problems.root_cause: quantify.md obligation 2 keys rules per tab construct («per formula group one rule keyed by output»); there is no concept of a rule that spans lines/tabs with the line as a binding, so identical business logic is minted once per tab.

problems.title: Excel conditional formatting is mandated as facts by the spec — 9 of 81 entries, colours not even captured
problems.evidence: quantify.md line 82-83: "per conditional-format rule a flag rule with its threshold constant". Produced T-4073..T-4081 = 9 entries, e.g. T-4074 «قاعده قالب‌بندی شرطی روی محدوده L6:L15 تب پیتزا که سلول‌های بزرگ‌تر از صفر را متمایز می‌کند … قالب رنگی در استخراج ثبت نشده است» ("…the colour format was not recorded in the extraction"), and T-4073 «آستانه در هر هشت قاعده صفر است» ("the threshold is zero in all eight rules"). The source dump cf.tsv is 9 lines with an empty `format` column.
problems.root_cause: The spec turns a presentation feature into a fact kind, and the dump does not even carry the format, so the entries encode nothing but 'someone coloured cells above/below zero'.

problems.title: Spreadsheet plumbing recorded as business facts
problems.evidence: T-4002 `gozaresh_markazi__refresher`: a hidden one-cell tab whose entire content is the unix-ms timestamp `1783786014375`, recorded as a `record` with a field and a row. T-4008 `sheets_file_ids`: 7 Google file IDs as a reference record. T-4024 `onOpen` («منوی Actions با گزینه Recalculate All را اضافه می‌کند»). T-4025 `triggerRecalculation`. T-4001 `form_responses_1` — a tab the agent itself describes as having only a header row and an "Untitled Question", tagged `issues: [{kind: junk}]` — while quantify.md line 78 says "an empty tab yields nothing".
problems.root_cause: The spec's walk is structural ("per non-empty tab one record", "one rule lang: gs per function") with no value filter, so mechanism is indistinguishable from business content.

problems.title: A quantitative-facts pass that produced no quantities: 0 items, 0 measurements, 0 notes
problems.evidence: Final delta kind counts: 73 `rule`, 8 `record`, 0 `item`, 0 `measurement`, 0 `note` (agent confirms: «۸ رکورد، ۷۳ قاعده، صفر قلم، صفر اندازه‌گیری، صفر یادداشت»). The only numeric business content is 5 tolerance constants (T-4026..T-4030, e.g. «تلورانس ۵ گرم به ازای هر پرس فروخته‌شده»). Roughly 14 of 81 entries (17%) carry non-duplicated business content.
problems.root_cause: The dump for these tabs contains formulas but no values (see the rows.tsv gap), so there is nothing to measure; the pass degenerates into transcribing spreadsheet machinery.

problems.title: Engine dump gap: rows.tsv carries no rows for the report tabs, so records have no primary key
problems.evidence: attachments/sheets/.dump/1shXFbKyvEkpA…/rows.tsv is 77 lines and its sheet column contains only `SheetsFileIDs` (7) and `Table_Ingredients_*` (69) — zero rows for پیتزا/فرنگی/سوخاری/کانتر/تاریخ/Refresher/Form Responses 1. Agent (18:26:10Z): "the four report tabs' row-label column is not in the dump (column A is empty and `rows.tsv` covers only the reference tabs). Rather than invent a column, I set `primaryKey: []`." T-4004/5/6/7 all ship with `primaryKey: []` and 10/9/6/5 rows keyed only by an invented `key`.
problems.root_cause: `dump-workbook` exports row values only for tabs it classifies as reference/BOM; formula-driven report tabs get formulas.tsv (with a single `cached` snapshot) and nothing else, so their row identity is unrecoverable.

problems.title: 12 of 39 cross-part references point to entries the agent never read — correct only by luck
problems.evidence: The agent read facts-delta-B1.json in 6 chunks covering lines 1–1339 and 1355–1514. B1's ids by line: T-1035 at 1509, T-1036 at 1556, T-1050 at 2203. The delta references T-1036, T-1037, T-1038, T-1039, T-1040, T-1041, T-1045, T-1046, T-1047, T-1048, T-1049, T-1050 — all beyond line 1514. I verified all 39 external refs resolve correctly against B1/B2/B3 (0 dangling), so the extrapolation from the ##code numbering happened to be right.
problems.root_cause: Cross-part temp-id referencing requires reading megabyte-scale sibling deltas that blow the Read token cap, so the agent pattern-matches the numbering instead. A single reordering in B1 would have produced 12 silently wrong item links.

problems.title: Sequential batching was bolted onto an agent that has no batch mode
problems.evidence: quantify.md documents exactly three modes (`manifest`, `full`, `targeted`) and says full mode writes `{run_dir}/facts-delta.json`. The B4 dispatch overrides all of it in prose: "## IMPORTANT — this is a PARTIAL pass (batch 4 of 8)", a private temp-id block ("use only the 4000-block"), "Read the previous passes first", "Never re-propose an item or dish an earlier part minted", "Where a formula reads a `Table_*` tab that batch 5 will define, `ref` a stub or leave the cross-record link to the natural key".
problems.root_cause: The split was an emergency response to the full-mode crash, so every coordination invariant lives in an ad-hoc dispatch message with no schema, no check, and no way for the agent to verify it obeyed them.

problems.title: A spec deviation was ratified mid-run, desynchronising batches from each other
problems.evidence: Coordinator fix message (21:35:12): "**Keep your granularity decision** (one rule per column, cells in `bindings`) — it is fine, and part B6 mirrored it for the ناهارخوران twin, so changing it now would desynchronise the branches." quantify.md obligation 2 requires one rule per formula group. B1–B3 and B5/B7/B8 were not told to change.
problems.root_cause: Batches were dispatched before the grain question was settled, so the store now holds the same construct at two different grains depending on which batch wrote it, and the spec matches neither consistently.

problems.title: `data` is an unconstrained object, so 21 invented keys entered the store unvalidated
problems.evidence: schemas/facts-delta.schema.json line 98: `"data": { "type": "object" }`, with per-kind `required` keys only. Keys actually present in the 81 entries: medium(8), role(8), location(8), grain(8), primaryKey(8), fields(8), rows(6), row_meta(4), foreignKeys(1), lang(67), original(67), inputs(73), outputs(73), calls(35), edge_cases(15), expr(38), port(10), of(5), bindings(20), applies_to(10), precision(2). Of these, `bindings`, `row_meta`, `applies_to`, `precision` and `primaryKey` appear zero times in quantify.md or the quantify SKILL.md.
problems.root_cause: Nothing constrains `data`, so the agent invents structure to carry information the contract has no home for — and the fix round used that hole deliberately (see next item).

problems.title: Validator pressure laundered data out of a validated field into an invented one
problems.evidence: 74 errors of the form "row 'X' member 'Y' is not a declared field". The agent's fix (18:26:10Z): "`sheet_row`, `of`, `codes` and `items` moved out of `rows[]` into a sibling `data.row_meta[]` keyed by `row`, so no information was lost". T-4004 pre-fix row: `{"key":"item_1","title":"پنیر پیتزا","sheet_row":6,"unit":"kg","of":{"ref":"T-1001"}}`; post-fix row `{"key":"item_1","title":"پنیر پیتزا","unit":"kg"}` plus `row_meta: [{"row":"item_1","sheet_row":6,"of":{"ref":"T-1001"}}]`. The item→row links now live in a key no schema or validator knows about.
problems.root_cause: A strict rule on one field next to a wide-open sibling (`data`) makes relocation the cheapest fix; the error disappears and the referential integrity becomes unenforceable.

problems.title: Dump and part files routinely exceed the 25K-token Read cap, and the agent has no Grep
problems.evidence: Three consecutive failed Reads at 19:19:18/19:19:21/19:19:25 on facts-delta-B3.json: "File content (62263 tokens) exceeds maximum allowed tokens (25000)", then 55856, then 37171; the agent settled for `offset:1, limit:40` and read 40 of B3's 7,834 lines. Three `read_truncation_notice` attachments: sheets.json "showing lines 1-2745 of 3549 (27472 tokens, cap 25000)", formulas.tsv "1-143 of 207", cooking-030.json "1-1150 of 1814". Each banner advises "…or Grep to find a specific section" — Grep is not in the agent's toolset.
problems.root_cause: Artefact sizes (a 7,834-line delta, a 3,548-line sheets.json) were designed without regard to the reader's token cap, and the toolset omits the one tool the harness itself recommends for that situation.

problems.title: Truncated reads were never paged: 803 lines of sheets.json and 664 lines of cooking-030.json unread
problems.evidence: sheets.json read once at 19:18:11 (lines 1-2745 of 3549), never re-read; the unread tail contains `Table_Fried_Last`, `Table_Pizza_First`, `Table_Pizza_Request`, `Table_Pizza_Last`, `Table_Farangi_Request`, `Table_Farangi_Last` — the very tables its own rules reference. cooking-030.json read once at 19:20:52 (lines 1-1150 of 1814), never re-read. rows.tsv read once with `limit: 60` of 77 lines, never completed. Only formulas.tsv was actually paged (offset 144 at 19:18:20).
problems.root_cause: Paging is left to the model's discretion with no accounting; the banner's "Do NOT answer from this page alone" is advisory and the agent moved on. problems.title: The 94-minute sequential gap destroyed the prompt cache; the fix round re-ingested ~300K tokens at write price

problems.title: The agent did not follow the fix message's explicit first instruction

problems.title: The whole 103KB file was re-emitted to change 71 entries, though the targeting itself was correct

problems.title: An empty tab produced an entry despite the spec forbidding it

problems.title: The same 180-character process quote is duplicated verbatim across four entries
problems.evidence: T-4037, T-4049, T-4061, T-4070 each carry an identical `source` entry: `{"type":"process","ref":"departments/cooking/processes/cooking-030.json","node":"cooking-030-n016","quote":"بخش‌ها میزان مصرف را اعلام نمی‌کنند؛ …"}`. summary: B5 is the "healthy" batch — it never crashed, never hit the output cap, took 13m02s, and produced a schema-valid 50-entry delta on the first try — and it is still a total loss in value terms: all 50 entries are `record`s, 35 of them `role: mirror` and 15 `stub`, zero items/measurements/rules/notes, and every one of the 50 `statement` strings describes spreadsheet plumbing (hidden tab, IMPORT_FROM_SHEET, A:S range, named range $A:$M) while not one names a unit or carries a quantity. That is precisely the user's "mirror tables recorded at all" and "statements that cite sheet cells/tabs" complaint, and the coordinator's dispatch prompt explicitly ordered it ("most of this pass is thirty-odd small mirror records"). Three defects were baked in before the agent ran: (a) the agent prompt's QF-20 stub rule ("scope the workbook's manifest row") directly contradicts the engine's QF-43 check in apply.py:334, guaranteeing that all 15 stubs would be rejected — they were later blanked to `departments: []`; (b) the same agent prompt forbids a `foreignKeys` member on a mirror, yet the agent put one on all 35 and its own summary brags about it, and the engine's content.py validator had a hole that accepted the IMPORT-shaped member, later requiring a whole new `repair_foreign_keys` engine verb (commit 4a513f5) to clean up 84 such members estate-wide, 35 of them from this batch; (c) obligation 2 also requires "the rule that performs the pull" per IMPORT_FROM_SHEET and the agent wrote zero rules. Mechanically, the agent read 22 times over 10 files, skipped B2 entirely, saw only 60 of 169 lines of B4 (a Read-cap truncation it never paged past, so 53 of 81 prior entries were invisible for QF-34 dedup), and never opened three declared inputs — facts/.index.json (316 KB), the 36 cooking process files, and the .gs script. It planned nothing on paper, spent 3m32s in one silent thinking turn, then emitted the entire 62.5 KB delta in a single 341-second Write of 38,184 output tokens (94% of the run's output in one unretryable call), and could not self-check because its tool list is Read/Glob/Write with no Bash. The one genuinely valuable thing it found — 12 `column_shift` issues showing named ranges silently truncating ingredient columns to zero — is buried inside `issues[]` of the very mirror records that should be deleted, and the check was applied inconsistently: at least six identical truncations (table_pizza_first, table_farangi_first, table_sales_data_italian_pizza, table_sales_data_sandwich, table_ingredients_american_pizza, table_sales_data_steak) went unflagged. Cost: 22 API turns, 2.67M cache-read + 459K cache-create + 40.6K output tokens, context growing 17.7K → 254K, to process about 21.6 KB of actual input signal.

problems.root_cause: QF-19 obligation 2 in .claude/agents/quantify.md:74-88 mandates one record per non-empty tab, mirrors included. The spec models the spreadsheet's topology instead of the restaurant's quantities; the coordinator faithfully sharded that spec into batches. A mirror should be a reference on the source record (one field), not an entry.

problems.title: Agent-prompt stub-scope rule contradicts the engine's QF-43 check — 15 of 50 entries invalid by construction
problems.evidence: .claude/agents/quantify.md §Stubs (QF-20): "**Record stub** … `scope` the workbook's manifest row (`departments`/`branches`)". Manifest rows: Anbar markazi = departments ["warehouse"], Tedade Fooroosh markazi = ["cashier"]. The agent obeyed: T-5001..T-5004 scope departments ["warehouse"], T-5005..T-5015 ["cashier"]. engine/merge_facts/apply.py:334-335 rejects exactly this: `if not set(entry["scope"]["departments"]) <= {run_dept}: out.append(f"entry {…} scoped to another department")`. SKILL.md:661 states the opposite of the agent prompt: "it may not **create** facts scoped to that department (QF-43)". Diff of the written delta vs the on-disk facts-delta-B5.json shows all 15 stubs later patched to `"departments": []`.
problems.root_cause: Two authoritative documents disagree and the agent only reads one of them. quantify.md is the agent's prompt; SKILL.md is the coordinator playbook the agent never sees. The engine enforces the SKILL.md version.

problems.title: foreignKeys on all 35 mirrors — explicitly forbidden by the agent prompt, silently accepted by the engine validator, later required a dedicated repair verb
problems.evidence: .claude/agents/quantify.md:87-89: "per `IMPORT_FROM_SHEET` a `mirror_of` and the rule that performs the pull — **never a `foreignKeys` member**, which QF-9 gives a mirror no `fields[]` to build one from." The agent put one on every mirror: `"foreignKeys":[{"spreadsheetId":"1dmH8tCq…","sheet":"موجودی اول شب","range":"A:S","target":{"ref":"T-1058"}}]`, and its own Persian summary at 20:14:59 states it as an achievement: "۳۵ رکورد آینه (role: mirror، بدون fields[]، هرکدام با mirror_of و **یک ردیف foreignKeys**)". engine/merge_facts/content.py:372-378 documents the consequence verbatim: "**84 stored records carried an IMPORT descriptor here instead** (`{spreadsheetId, sheet, range, target}`), and the membership loop below read `fk.get(\"fields\") or []`, so an absent `fields` was an empty list and every one of them passed this pass cleanly." Cleanup cost: new engine verb `repair_foreign_keys` in engine/merge_facts/verbs.py:219, commit 4a513f5 "a verb that removes, because the ladder never can".
problems.root_cause: Twofold. (1) The dispatch prompt restated obligation 2 in abbreviated form and dropped the 'never a foreignKeys member' clause, so the operative instruction in front of the agent omitted the prohibition. (2) content.py's membership loop used `fk.get("fields") or []`, so a member with no `fields` key validated vacuously — a validator hole that turned a prompt violation into 84 stored defects.

problems.title: Zero rules produced — the second half of obligation 2 was silently dropped
problems.evidence: quantify.md:87 requires "per `IMPORT_FROM_SHEET` a `mirror_of` **and the rule that performs the pull**". 35 IMPORT_FROM_SHEET formulas in formulas.tsv → 0 rules. The agent's own summary: "همه از نوع record (۰ قلم، ۰ اندازه‌گیری، ۰ قاعده، ۰ یادداشت)". The dispatch prompt never mentioned rules at all.
problems.root_cause: The coordinator's per-batch prompt paraphrased the obligation and kept only the mirror-record half. Nothing downstream cross-checks a batch's output kinds against the obligations that batch was supposed to discharge.

problems.title: Three declared inputs never opened — including facts/.index.json, which QF-19 obligation 1 makes mandatory
problems.evidence: Dispatch "## Inputs" lists `process_paths: departments/cooking/processes/*.json` and `facts_index: facts/.index.json`. Full tool-call list (25 calls) contains neither. facts/.index.json is 316,035 bytes; departments/cooking/processes/ holds 36 files. quantify.md obligation 1: "Load the index and the in-scope entries; build the map of keys and titles it must reuse (QF-34)." Consequence visible in the output: `processes: []` on all 50 entries, and the agent's summary excuses it — "هیچ پیوند فرایندی هم افزوده نشد (این تب‌ها لوله‌کشی پنهان‌اند و هیچ گره فرایندی نامشان را نمی‌برد)" — a claim it could not have verified, having read none of the 36 process files.
problems.root_cause: Inputs are listed as prose paths with no manifest check, no required-read gate, and no post-run assertion. facts/.index.json at 316 KB is also physically unreadable under the 25K-token Read cap, so obligation 1 is impossible to discharge as written — the agent's rational move was to skip it, and nothing noticed.

problems.title: Read-cap truncation left B4 read at 36% and B2 unread — QF-34 duplicate avoidance was impossible
problems.evidence: Attachment at transcript line 32: "[Truncated: PARTIAL view — …facts-delta-B4.json: showing lines 1-60 of 169 total (59429 tokens, cap 25000). Call Read with offset=61 … for the next page]". The agent never issued that follow-up: B4 appears exactly once in the tool list (call #10, 20:02:39). T-ids visible anywhere in its context: T-4001..T-4028 only — 28 of B4's 81 entries, and none of B4's 73 rules. facts-delta-B2.json was never read at all despite the dispatch's "**Read the previous passes first** (`.../parts/facts-delta-B1.json` … `B4.json`)" and its reference to "their ناهارخوران twins" as mirror_of candidates. Two other files were truncated and correctly paged (sheets.json 3549 lines, formulas.tsv 207 lines).
problems.root_cause: Prior parts are monolithic JSON blobs with no index, so the only access pattern is blind offset paging against a 25K-token cap. The coordinator gave the agent no key→temp-id map, forcing 11 exploratory offset reads across B1/B3 and leaving B4/B2 uncovered.

problems.title: One 62.5 KB Write at the end — 94% of the run's output in a single 341-second unretryable call
problems.evidence: Tool call #25 at 20:13:54: Write facts-delta-B5.json, content length 62,554 chars. The turn ran 20:08:13→20:13:54 (341 s) with output_tokens=38,184; the run's total output is 40,641, so this one call is 94%. No outline, no plan file, no per-tab incremental writes, no checkpoint. Kinds/counts were decided inside that one uninspectable stream.
problems.root_cause: The output contract is a single file at a single path ({run_dir}/facts-delta.json, quantify.md §Output contract) and the agent's only writing tool is Write, which overwrites. There is no append mode and no per-entry sink, so a 50-entry delta must be one atomic emission — which is also exactly the shape that hits max_output_tokens in the larger batches.

problems.title: The agent structurally cannot validate its own output — tools are Read, Glob, Write with no Bash
problems.evidence: .claude/agents/quantify.md frontmatter: `tools: Read, Glob, Write`. All 25 tool calls are Read/Glob/Write; zero Bash. It read the schema (call #1, 6,617 bytes, untruncated) and then produced 62.5 KB of JSON against it from memory. It never re-read the written file — the Write result even says "file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back". It could not run `merge facts apply --check`, could not run `python -m json.tool`, could not count its own entries.
problems.root_cause: Deliberate tool restriction (INV-1/QF-2: the agent must not touch facts/**) implemented as a blanket Bash ban rather than an allowlisted read-only validator command. The cost is that every structural error survives to the coordinator's concatenation step, which is where the 2,068 errors surfaced.

problems.title: The schema does not constrain `data` at all — every invented shape validates
problems.evidence: code-repo/schemas/facts-delta.schema.json line 98: `"data": { "type": "object" }`. The agent invented `data.import{file_id_named_range, source_sheet, range}`, `data.named_range{name, refers_to}`, `data.foreignKeys[{spreadsheetId, sheet, range, target}]`, `data.mirror_of`, `data.stub`, `role: "mirror"` — none of these appear anywhere in the schema (grep for "mirror"/"foreignKeys" in the schema returns nothing). The only `data` constraint in the whole file is on one nested sub-shape at line 105: `"data": { "type": "object", "required": ["medium","role","location"] }`.
problems.root_cause: The data contract was frozen at the envelope level only; the payload shape lives entirely in prose in quantify.md. Consistency across eight independently-prompted batches therefore rests on prose recall, and JSON-Schema validation gives false confidence.

problems.title: Zero quantitative content: 50/50 entries are records about spreadsheet plumbing, 0 name a unit
problems.evidence: Programmatic scan of the written delta: kinds = Counter({'record': 50}); roles = {mirror: 35, log: 15}; entries with fields[] = 0; with rows[] = 0; with accounts[] = 0; with processes[] = 0. Statements matching /تب |Table_|\.xlsx|ستون [A-Z]|A:[A-Z]|IMPORT_FROM_SHEET/ = 50/50. Statements naming any unit (کیلوگرم|گرم|عدد|ریال|تومان|درصد) = 0/50. Store-wide the pattern holds: 139 items + 156 records + 156 rules + 22 notes but only **13 measurements** across 486 entries (2.7%).
problems.root_cause: The unit of extraction is 'a tab' rather than 'a quantity'. A one-formula mirror tab has no quantity in it, so a spec that demands one entry per tab necessarily manufactures a non-quantitative fact for every such tab.

problems.title: The truncated-range check was applied inconsistently — at least six identical defects went unflagged
problems.evidence: Per-mirror table of import range vs named range: table_ingredients_italian_pizza (A:X vs $A:$V) → 1 issue, but table_ingredients_american_pizza (A:X vs $A:$V, identical shape) → 0 issues. table_sales_data_italian_pizza (A:X vs $A:$O) → 0; table_sales_data_sandwich (A:X vs $A:$O) → 0; table_sales_data_steak (A:C vs $A:$B) → 0. problems.root_cause: No per-tab checklist and no loop structure: the 35 tabs were handled inside one 341-second free-form generation. Whether a given tab got the check depended on where attention happened to fall in the stream. This is the failure mode a per-tab write (or a deterministic pre-computed range-diff table in the dispatch) would have eliminated.

problems.title: The batch's only real findings are trapped inside the entries that should be deleted
problems.evidence: 19 issues across 18 entries: 12 column_shift, 3 junk, 2 code_collision, 1 unit_kind, 1 bug. Several are genuinely valuable — e.g. T-5046: "محدوده وارداتی «A:E» شش ستون کمتر از تب مبدأ است … در نتیجه ردیف «قارچ سوخاری #5» در این آینه کاملاً صفر است، در حالی که در مبدأ ۳۵۰ قارچ سوخاری … دارد" (a silent zeroing of 350 g of mushrooms per portion in the deviation report). All 19 live in `issues[]` on mirror records; deleting the mirrors deletes the findings.
problems.root_cause: `issues[]` is a sub-object of an entry rather than a first-class kind. Findings therefore inherit the lifetime and the deletability of whatever plumbing entry happened to be under the cursor when they were noticed.

problems.title: Cross-batch leakage: a finding about B4's tab attached to a B5 record
problems.evidence: T-5048 (gozaresh_markazi__table_ingredients_starter) carries issue kind `bug`: "سلول‌های I9 و K9 و I13 و K13 تب «فرنگی» گزارش، مصرف اقلام ##23 و ##22 را برای غذای شماره ۴ در همین جدول جست‌وجو می‌کنند … نتیجه رشته «ID not found» و سپس خطای #NUM!". The «فرنگی» tab of the report workbook is a non-Table_* tab, i.e. B4's assignment (record gozaresh_markazi__farangi, T-4005), not B5's. The dispatch explicitly scoped B5 to "**only its `Table_*` tabs**".
problems.root_cause: Batch boundaries are drawn on tabs, but real defects live in the join between tabs. A finding that spans the boundary has no correct home, so it lands wherever it was noticed — making a boundary-based sharding scheme unsound for anything relational.

problems.title: Verification over-claimed: 'cell-by-cell identical' asserted for rows never in context
problems.evidence: T-5039 statement: "مقادیر آورده‌شده سلول‌به‌سلول با رکورد مرجع مبدأ یکی‌اند", and the final summary generalises it to all twelve: "مقایسه سلول‌به‌سلول دوازده تب نسخه با رکوردهای مرجع پاس سوم نشان داد هر مقداری که آینه می‌آورد دقیقاً با مبدأ یکی است". Cross-checking B3's 69 reference rows against every tool_result in the transcript: 65 were visible, 4 never were — dish_71, dish_309, dish_74, dish_65, all in mavade_avalie__pitza_americai (12 rows, 4 unseen), the very record T-5039 mirrors.
problems.root_cause: Coverage of a sampled read is invisible to the agent — offset paging gives no 'you have seen N of M entries' signal, so a partial read feels complete. Nothing in the output contract asks for a coverage statement, only a conclusion.

problems.title: The ponytail 'lazy developer / YAGNI / write less' persona was injected into a data-extraction agent
problems.evidence:
Transcript attachments at lines 1-2: `{"type":"hook_success","hookName":"SubagentStart:quantify", … "PONYTAIL MODE ACTIVE — level: full

# Ponytail

You are a lazy senior developer … 1. **Does this need to exist at all?** Speculative need = skip it … Deletion over addition … Shortest working diff wins"}`.
