Not provably causal, but it is a systematic pressure toward exactly the behaviours observed here — skipping B2, skipping the 316 KB index, skipping 36 process files, one terse pass, no re-read — inside an agent whose job is exhaustive extraction.

problems.title: Bootstrap order violated: the report workbook was processed before the workbooks it points at, manufacturing 15 stubs
problems.evidence: SKILL.md:655-659: "Then the universal seeds under `management` (QF-43), then station and warehouse workbooks, then sales and ingredients, then **the report workbooks**, so cross-workbook references resolve to real records and **few stubs are left to fill**." This run is department-scoped to cooking and included Gozaresh markazi.xlsx (a report workbook) while Anbar markazi.xlsx (warehouse) and Tedade Fooroosh markazi.xlsx (cashier) had no entries — producing 15 stubs, i.e. 30% of the batch, each of which then hit the QF-43 contradiction.
problems.root_cause: The bootstrap ordering is documented per-estate but the run driver is per-department. A cooking run cannot honour an estate-wide ordering that requires warehouse and cashier to be seeded first.

problems.title: The mandated Persian return summary cost a full 254K-token cache re-creation
problems.evidence: Dispatch "## Return" demands "counts per kind, every `unknown` field, every disputed field with its accounts verbatim, every stub created, the data issues found, and **the full list of `key`s you minted plus the earlier-pass keys you reused**". Result: 5,375 chars of Persian at 20:14:59, largely a verbatim re-listing of the 50 keys already in the file. Its usage block: `cache_creation_input_tokens: 253966, cache_read_input_tokens: 0` — the 341-second Write blew the 5-minute ephemeral cache TTL, so the entire 254K context was re-created rather than read on the very next turn.
problems.root_cause: The summary duplicates information the file already contains and the coordinator could compute deterministically, and it is demanded on the turn immediately after the longest possible generation — the worst point in the run for cache economics.

problems.title: 3.13M prompt tokens and 22 API turns to process ~21.6 KB of actual signal
problems.evidence: Per-message accounting: 22 assistant turns; output 40,641; cache_read 2,673,139; cache_creation 458,924; input 43. Context grew 17,702 → 253,968 tokens (14×) over 13m02s. The genuinely load-bearing input is 35 lines of formulas.tsv (~4.5 KB), names.tsv (4,254 B) and rows.tsv (12,879 B) ≈ 21.6 KB. Total tool_result text pulled into context: 312,307 chars, most of it sheets.json's 43-tab structure and 250-odd lines of prior-part JSON sampled blind.
problems.root_cause: The agent must reconstruct cross-batch state (key→temp-id maps, prior-part contents) by reading whole JSON blobs, because the coordinator passes no digest. Each blind offset read is a permanent context addition that every later turn re-pays for.

problems.title: Stubs carry invented fields despite the 'nothing but identity' rule
problems.evidence: quantify.md §Stubs: "both the one exception to 'a run only writes what it read', and both writing **nothing but identity**". T-5001 data keys are ['medium','role','location','stub'] with `role: "log"` and `field_status: {"data/role": "inferred"}` — a guessed role on a workbook the agent states in the same statement it did not read: "خود فایل در این پاس خوانده نشده و ساختار ستون‌هایش اینجا ثبت نشده است".
problems.root_cause: 'Nothing but identity' is not enumerated as an allowed key set, and the schema's unconstrained `data` object cannot enforce one, so the agent filled in the fields the shape 'felt' like it needed.

problems.title: The stub fix left 15 orphan entries scoped to no department at all
problems.evidence: Diff of the agent's Write against the on-disk facts-delta-B5.json: the only change across all 50 entries is `"departments": ["warehouse"|"cashier"] → []` on the 15 stubs. In facts/records.json F-00187 (anbar_markazi__pitza) now reads `"scope": {"departments": [], "branches": ["chalebagh"]}`. Per apply.py QF-43 an empty department scope means universal, so 15 warehouse/cashier plumbing stubs are now estate-wide entries owned by nobody.
problems.root_cause: The fix targeted the validator message rather than the modelling question. A cross-department reference has no correct scope under QF-43 as written, so the only passing value is the semantically wrong one.

problems.title: 22 Read calls over 10 files, 14 of them blind offset probes, because prior parts have no index
problems.evidence: Call list: sheets.json ×2, formulas.tsv ×2, B1 ×5 (offsets 100/860/690/920/1250), B3 ×6 (offsets 1/180/148/210/340/123/122 — including two 1-2-line pinpoint probes at 20:08:00 and 20:08:05 purely to confirm that T-3088 = mavade_avalie__pitza_americai before extrapolating T-3089..T-3099). Only meta.json, names.tsv, rows.tsv, manifest.json and the schema were read once and whole. cf.tsv (344 B), validations.tsv (333 B) and comments.tsv (23 B) were listed by the Glob at 20:02:38 and never opened.
problems.root_cause: The coordinator hands over 'read B1..B4' with no key→id map and no per-part index, so temp-id resolution becomes a binary search through megabytes of JSON under a 25K-token Read cap.

details:
## 0. Verdict up front

B5 is the control case. It did **not** crash, did **not** hit `max_output_tokens` (40,641 output tokens total against a 64K cap), did **not** receive a fix message, finished in 13m02s, and its delta merged cleanly (all 50 temp ids appear in `id-map.json`). It is still 100% low-value output. **The failure in this batch is not the crash — it is the specification.**

Transcript: `/home/lili/.claude/projects/-home-lili-Desktop-DriveD-work-Moshtaghi-Inja-food-process-process-dev-data-repo/ffa1efdd-cf44-4caa-b4e3-9b3853970a43/subagents/agent-a9335cfe8668323f9.jsonl` (79 lines, 646,869 B; 48 assistant records = 22 API turns, 26 user records, 5 attachments). Extracted written delta saved to `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-lili-Desktop-DriveD-work-Moshtaghi-Inja-food-process-process-dev-code-repo/e5187b82-c412-4e53-b8cb-e5802c91a5c1/scratchpad/B5_written.json`; digest at `.../scratchpad/b5.digest.txt`.

**Note on evidence limits:** every `thinking` block in this transcript has `"thinking": ""` with only a `signature` — reasoning content is not persisted. So there are no self-doubt/complaint quotes to mine (item 4 of the brief). What the agent struggled with has to be read off its behaviour, its output, and its final summary.

---

## 1. Inputs handed over vs. what it actually read

Dispatch prompt: 4,807 chars. Declared inputs:

| Declared input | Size | Read? |
|---|---|---|
| `schemas/facts-delta.schema.json` | 6,617 B | ✅ full, call #1 |
| `.dump/1shXFbK…/sheets.json` | 70,063 B | ✅ 2 calls (truncated at line 2745/3549, paged) |
| `.dump/…/formulas.tsv` | 48,980 B | ✅ 2 calls (truncated at 143/207, paged) |
| `.dump/…/names.tsv` | 4,254 B | ✅ full |
| `.dump/…/rows.tsv` | 12,879 B | ✅ full |
| `.dump/…/meta.json` | 742 B | ✅ full |
| `.dump/…/cf.tsv` | 344 B | ❌ globbed 20:02:38, never opened |
| `.dump/…/validations.tsv` | 333 B | ❌ globbed, never opened |
| `.dump/…/comments.tsv` | 23 B | ❌ globbed, never opened |
| `attachments/sheets/manifest.json` | — | ✅ full |
| `parts/facts-delta-B1.json` | 142,501 B | ⚠️ 5 offset reads (100/860/690/920/1250) |
| `parts/facts-delta-B2.json` | 76,655 B | ❌ **never read** |
| `parts/facts-delta-B3.json` | 193,160 B | ⚠️ 6 offset reads |
| `parts/facts-delta-B4.json` | 164,816 B | ⚠️ **1 read, truncated at line 60 of 169, never paged** |
| `facts/.index.json` | 316,035 B | ❌ **never read** (obligation 1 requires it) |
| `departments/cooking/processes/*.json` | 36 files | ❌ **never read** |
| `Gozaresh markazi.gs` | — | ❌ never read (dispatch made it optional) |

**Read-call arithmetic:** 22 Read + 2 Glob + 1 Write = 25 tool calls, 0 errors. 22 Reads over **10 distinct files**; **12 are re-reads** of a file already touched (sheets.json ×2, formulas.tsv ×2, B1 ×5, B3 ×6). **14 of 22 carry an explicit `offset`**; 3 more were silently truncated by the 25K-token cap.

**Coverage of prior parts, measured by which temp ids ever entered context** (regex over all tool_result text): T-1007-1009, T-1044-1066 (25 of B1's 67) · **none of B2's 18** · T-3001-3006 + T-3088-3100 (19 of B3's 100) · T-4001-4028 (**28 of B4's 81**). B4's 73 rules were never visible, so QF-34 rule-duplication checking against the immediately preceding batch of the same workbook was impossible.

The actually load-bearing input for this batch is tiny: **35 lines of `formulas.tsv`** (one `IMPORT_FROM_SHEET` per tab, ~120 chars each), `names.tsv` (4.2 KB) and `rows.tsv` (12.9 KB) — ≈ **21.6 KB**. Total tool_result text pulled into context: **312,307 chars**.

---

## 2. Wall-clock timeline (Tehran, 2026-09-02)

| Stage | Start | End | Dur | What |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dispatch received | 20:01:57 | — | — | 4,807-char prompt |
| A. Schema + workbook dump | 20:01:59 | 20:02:31 | 32 s | schema, sheets.json ×2, formulas.tsv ×2, meta.json, names.tsv |
| B. Orientation | 20:02:31 | 20:02:52 | 21 s | 2 Globs, B4 (truncated), manifest.json |
| C. B1 sampling | 20:03:13 | 20:03:39 | 26 s | 5 blind offset reads |
| D. B3 sampling + rows.tsv | 20:03:47 | 20:04:26 | 39 s | 4 offset reads + rows.tsv full |
| **E. SILENT GAP** | **20:04:26** | **20:07:58** | **3 m 32 s** | one turn, thinking only, 2 visible output tokens, no tool call |
| F. Pinpoint id probes | 20:07:58 | 20:08:05 | 7 s | B3 offset 123 limit 2, then offset 122 limit 1 — confirming `T-3088 = mavade_avalie__pitza_americai` |
| **G. The single Write** | **20:08:13** | **20:13:54** | **5 m 41 s** | 62,554 chars, **38,184 output tokens** in one call |
| H. Persian summary | 20:14:05 | 20:14:59 | 53 s | 5,375 chars; `cache_read: 0`, `cache_creation: 253,966` |
| **Total** | 20:01:57 | 20:14:59 | **13 m 02 s** | |

Reading = 2m29s (19%). Silent thinking = 3m32s (27%). Writing = 5m41s (44%). Summarising = 53s (7%). **Generation is 51% of wall clock.**

The 341-second Write is longer than the 5-minute ephemeral prompt-cache TTL, which is why turn H shows `cache_read_input_tokens: 0` alongside `cache_creation_input_tokens: 253,966` — the whole 254K context was re-created at write price.

---

## 3. How it built the delta

- **No plan, no outline, no scratch file.** It went straight from reading to one Write.
- **One giant Write**, tool call #25, 62,554 chars, 50 entries → 1,251 chars/entry.
- **No self-check possible.** `.claude/agents/quantify.md` frontmatter: `tools: Read, Glob, Write`. No Bash → no `merge facts apply --check`, no `python -m json.tool`, no `jq`, no entry count. It read the schema at 20:02:00 and then wrote 62.5 KB against it from memory 12 minutes later.
- **It never re-read its own output.** The Write tool result explicitly discourages it: *"file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back."*
- The two pinpoint reads at F (1 and 2 lines of B3) show it *did* care about ref correctness — it verified `T-3088` and then extrapolated `T-3089..T-3099` by tab order. That extrapolation happened to be correct; nothing verified it. Full ref audit of the written delta: 57 `ref` values, **0 dangling**, all 35 `mirror_of` targets resolve correctly against B1/B3/own. Referential integrity is the one thing this batch got right.

---

## 4. What it got wrong

No thinking text survives, so this is behavioural. Two things it *said*, both over-claims:

## 9. What a redesign should take from this batch specifically

1. **A mirror tab should produce no entry.** It should add one `mirrored_by` locator to the source record. That alone removes 70 of 156 store records.
2. **The 12 `column_shift` findings are the only output worth keeping.** They are computable deterministically — `named_range width vs import range width vs source tab dimension` is a three-column join over `names.tsv`, `formulas.tsv` and each source `sheets.json`. An engine check would find all ~20, not the 12 an LLM happened to notice. Give the agent the diff table, not the raw TSVs.
3. **A stub for a cross-department workbook has no valid scope under QF-43.** Either QF-43 gains an exception for `data.stub`, or stubs stop existing and the reference stays unresolved until that department's own run — which is what the SKILL.md bootstrap order already implies.
4. **Give the agent one read-only validator command** (Bash allowlisted to `merge facts apply --check`), or the coordinator validates each part before the next dispatch instead of concatenating eight unvalidated parts and discovering 2,068 errors at the end.
5. **Write per tab, not per batch.** 35 small writes cost the same tokens, survive a crash, and make the per-tab checklist structurally enforceable rather than attentional.

It spent only 2m52s reading (34 tool calls total: 23 Read, 7 Glob, 3 Write, 1 rejected Edit), then 12 min generating a valid 14-entry file and attempting to APPEND the rest with Edit — a correct incremental strategy that the harness rejected ("Edit is disabled for this session, in subagents as well as here"), forcing a full 19-min regeneration of a 104,510-char file that lands at ~99% of the 64,000 output-token cap. It had no Bash and no validator, so it could not self-check; the delta came back with 358 content errors, 260 of them from one contract fact (inputs/outputs members are keyed by `key`, not `name`) that is nowhere in `facts-delta.schema.json` — the only contract the dispatch pointed at. It diagnosed the contract correctly by reading the engine's TEST file (it never found `engine/merge_facts/content.py`; five Globs missed it), then burned 38.6 min and ~1.1M cache-creation tokens on three consecutive full-file rewrite attempts that all blew the 64K output cap and wrote nothing. Most of the low-value output is mandated verbatim by the quantify agent prompt's step 2 and blessed by the schema's `cf`/`validation` source types, not invented by this agent. problems.title: Pipeline-internal justifications leak into user-facing statements
problems.evidence: T-6008 fixed statement ends '… در زیرمجموعه FEEL قابل بیان نیست، بنابراین فقط متن اصلی فرمول ثبت شده است.'; T-6037 '… این جمع روی جدول‌های آینه فروش و نسخه اجرا می‌شود که هیچ‌کدام در این پاس تعریف نشده‌اند، بنابراین به‌جای صورت انبوهه تنها متن اصلی فرمول ثبت شده است.' The coordinator asked for this: 'drop `expr` and keep the verbatim `original`, saying in one sentence in `statement` why.'
problems.root_cause: `statement` is used both as the human-readable fact and as an audit log for the extraction agent's own limitations; no separate field exists for extraction metadata.

problems.title: 11 statements narrate the other branch's workbook — cross-batch comparison prose baked into facts
problems.evidence: T-6025 '… همان مقداری که در فایل گزارش شعبه چاله‌باغ هم آمده است.'; T-6026/6027/6028/6029 '… برابر با مقدار فایل گزارش شعبه چاله‌باغ.'; T-6053 'برخلاف تب هم‌نام فایل گزارش شعبه چاله‌باغ که این ستون را فقط برای شش ردیف وزنی (M9:M14) و با گرد کردن سه رقمی دارد …'; T-6001 'برخلاف فایل گزارش شعبه چاله‌باغ، سطر عنوان ردیف ۵ و سطر مقدار ردیف ۶ است.'
problems.root_cause: The dispatch demanded '**every place this workbook differs from its چاله‌باغ twin**' in the report, and the agent also encoded those diffs into the entries themselves.

problems.title: Colloquial spoken-register process prose pasted verbatim into four entries as evidence
problems.evidence: T-6036/6048/6060/6069 carry `"quote": "بخش‌ها میزان مصرف را اعلام نمی‌کنند؛ آن‌ها یک مانده اول شب دارند که همان مانده شب گذشته است و یک مانده آخر شب، و حسابداری از تفاضل این دو میزان مصرف را محاسبه می‌کند."` — sourced from cooking-030.json line 495, itself transcript-derived narration.
problems.root_cause: QF-8 requires a verbatim `quote` for a process link, and process node descriptions are spoken-register text, so the register propagates into the facts store unchanged.

problems.title: The QF-8 process-link contract (source ref must name the .json file) is undiscoverable and cost 4 errors
problems.evidence: errs_B6.txt: 4 × "processes[] link to 'cooking-0NN' has no process-type source naming its file". The agent wrote `{"type": "process", "ref": "cooking-030", "node": "cooking-030-n016", "quote": …}`; the fix required `"ref": "departments/cooking/processes/cooking-030.json"`. The schema's `source` definition (line 43) allows any string for `ref` and says nothing about the file-path form.
problems.root_cause: Same two-layer contract split: the shape is legal per schema, illegal per content.py.

problems.title: 74 'row member is not a declared field' errors from a rows/fields coupling with no schema expression
problems.evidence: errs_B6.txt lines 1-2: "T-6002: row 'refresher' member 'value' is not a declared field", "T-6002: row 'refresher' member 'cell' is not a declared field". Row member keys the agent actually wrote: Counter({'key': 38, 'title': 30, 'sheet_row': 30, 'unit': 30, 'of': 25, 'cell': 8, 'range_name': 7, 'sheets_file_id': 7, 'codes': 5, 'items': 5, 'value': 1}) — most of these are structural metadata, not table columns. The coordinator's own fix moved them to `data.row_meta[]`, a container the schema also does not mention.
problems.root_cause: `data` is `{type: object}` in the schema — completely free-form — while content.py enforces a specific rows↔fields discipline that only its source code states.

problems.title: Reading 5 files cost ~178K context tokens for a pass whose real inputs are ~50K; context peaked at 436K
problems.evidence: Truncation banners give per-file token estimates: facts-delta-B4.json 59,429; cooking-030.json 33,501; formulas.tsv 30,698; facts-delta-B2.json 28,505; sheets.json 26,073. Peak cache_creation_input_tokens 435,861 (final turn), peak cache_read 381,298. Total across the run: cache_read 5,107,192, cache_creation 3,312,578 over 35 unique assistant messages. sheets.json is one 3,325-line file for a 42-tab workbook, of which this batch owns lines 8-426 (its seven tabs) — the other ~2,900 lines are batch 7's.
problems.root_cause: The dump is per-workbook, not per-tab, and there is no Grep in the toolset, so a seven-tab batch must ingest a forty-two-tab file; the same file is re-ingested by every one of the eight sequential batches.

problems.title: 41 minutes of idle wall-clock between the agent finishing and the coordinator returning with errors
problems.evidence: Final report at 20:54:20; coordinator wake-up at 21:35:29 (gap 41.2 min). Second idle gap 22:17:41 → 22:22:18 (4.6 min). Of the 135-min span: ~3 min reading, ~38 min productive generation, ~39 min crashed generation, ~46 min idle.
problems.root_cause: Eight sequential batches concatenated and validated only as a whole, so no batch learns it is broken until every batch is finished.

problems.title: A PONYTAIL 'lazy senior developer' coding-persona hook is injected into the quantify data-extraction agent on every wake
problems.evidence: Transcript indices 2, 80, 112: attachment type 'hook_additional_context', hookName 'SubagentStart:quantify', 5,338 chars each, beginning 'PONYTAIL MODE ACTIVE — level: full … You are a lazy senior developer … The best code is the code never written.' It contains directives such as 'Deletion over addition', 'Shortest working diff wins', 'No boilerplate, no scaffolding for later'.
problems.root_cause: A SubagentStart hook with no agent-name filter fires for a non-coding agent, adding ~1.5K irrelevant tokens per wake and instructing an exhaustive-extraction agent to minimise output.

problems.title: Coordinator's second fix message did the agent's job for it, proving the split was mis-sized
problems.evidence: 22:22:18: 'I already applied every mechanical fix to B6 … every `inputs[]`/`outputs[]` member's `name` is now `key` and camelCase keys are snake_case … row members … moved from `rows[]` into a sibling `data.row_meta[]` … the four unresolvable `primaryKey`s are now `[]`; and the four `process`-type source `ref`s now name the file'. The remaining agent work then took 7.2 min and 64 entries.
problems.root_cause: 294 of the 358 errors were mechanical string rewrites that a script (or the agent, with Edit/Bash) could apply in seconds; routing them through a 64K-capped LLM regeneration cost ~39 min and two crashes.

problems.title: The agent never planned or outlined before writing; it went from last Read to a 12-minute generation with one sentence of intent
problems.evidence: Last input read 20:18:39 (cooking-030.json); 20:20:13 'Now I have everything. Writing the delta.'; first Write completes 20:32:12. No entry list, no id allocation plan, no size estimate. All thinking blocks in the transcript are empty (`{'type','thinking','signature'}` with thinking='').
problems.root_cause: Nothing in the agent prompt or dispatch asks for an outline/entry-count/size budget before generation, so the agent cannot notice it is about to exceed the output cap.

problems.title: Five duplicate tolerance constants across branches — the only real numbers in the pass are stated twice
problems.evidence: T-6025..T-6029 (5g, 140g, 4g, 75g, 100g) each with a statement ending 'برابر با مقدار فایل گزارش شعبه چاله‌باغ' — the agent explicitly notes each is identical to the چاله‌باغ entry B4 already wrote. The dispatch required it: 'Where a rule here is byte-identical in meaning to B4's چاله‌باغ rule, it still gets its own entry (a record/rule is per-workbook)'.
problems.root_cause: Facts are scoped per workbook rather than per rule-with-a-scope-list, so a rule that holds in both branches cannot be expressed once with `branches: [chalebagh, naharkhoran]`.

problems.title: Items minted in an earlier pass carry the wrong branch scope and the agent could only flag it, not fix it
problems.evidence: Agent's report 20:54:20: 'یک نکته برای بازبینی انسانی: مدخل‌های قلم پاس اول دامنه‌شان `chalebagh` است ولی همین کدها در این فایل ناهارخورانی هم به کار می‌روند؛ تصمیم درباره گشاد کردن دامنه آن اقلام با انسان است.' 39 distinct T-1xxx item refs are used from this naharkhoran-scoped delta.
problems.root_cause: Sequential batches cannot revise a predecessor's entries, so a scope error discovered in batch 6 has no repair path short of a human edit.

problems.title: Cell-comment and data-validation trivia are mandated as facts by the agent prompt
problems.evidence: quantify.md step 2: 'per validation a `constraints.enum`; per conditional-format rule a flag rule with its threshold constant; per cell comment a constant rule or note with `source.type: comment`'. In B6 this produced 3 `validation` source citations for the date dropdowns (تاریخ!C6 day list 1..31, D6 month names, E6 years 1403..1410) inside T-6001. comments.tsv here was empty (27 bytes), so B6 escaped the cell-comment trivia the user complained about elsewhere; the rule that generates it is unchanged.
problems.root_cause: The checklist enumerates spreadsheet features exhaustively; a dropdown list of the numbers 1-31 and a colour rule are treated with the same weight as a 140-gram tolerance.

## 3. How it built the delta

**No plan, no outline.** Last input read 20:18:39 → 20:20:13 `"Now I have everything. Writing the delta."` → 12 min of generation. No entry list, no id budget, no size estimate.

**It DID try to write incrementally.** Write #1 produced a *syntactically complete* 14-entry file ending `\n]\n}\n`, then Edit with `old_string: "\n]\n}\n"` and a 13,136-char `new_string` (T-6015..T-6024 + the closing bracket). Rejected: `Error: No such tool available: Edit. Edit is disabled for this session, in subagents as well as here.` Its response at 20:34:06: `"Edit is unavailable, so I must emit the whole file in one Write. Writing the complete 80-entry delta, compactly."`

**Self-check: impossible.** `tools: Read, Glob, Write` (quantify.md line 5). No Bash → cannot run `validate facts-delta`. It read the schema as its very first action and got nothing enforceable: the schema's rule branch is `data: {type: "object", required: ["inputs","outputs"]}` and `data` is otherwise `{type: object}`.

Sizes: 26,920 → 104,510 → 81,623 chars. Observed rate 1.59 chars/token (Write #1: 26,920 chars = 16,906 output tokens), putting Write #2 at ≈65K tokens — at the 64,000 cap.

## 4. What it struggled with (its own words)

- 21:36:50 — `"Every `expr` identifier was rejected, even plainly-declared ones. I need the validator's actual rule — let me find it."`
- 21:39:07 — `"Found it. The tests reveal the actual contract: `inputs[]`/`outputs[]` members are keyed by **`key`**, not `name` (that's why all 260 identifiers failed), and the identifier check only runs for `lang: \"feel\"`. Rewriting."` (diagnosed from `engine/tests/test_validate_facts_content.py` — it never located `engine/merge_facts/content.py`)
- 22:31:03, refusing to fabricate — `"One thing I deliberately did **not** do: express «مصرف واقعی» with the aggregate form … their temp ids and field keys are not knowable here, and inventing them would be fabrication (INV-3)."`
- 20:54:20, flagging a predecessor's scope error it cannot fix — `"مدخل‌های قلم پاس اول دامنه‌شان `chalebagh` است ولی همین کدها در این فایل ناهارخورانی هم به کار می‌روند؛ تصمیم درباره گشاد کردن دامنه آن اقلام با انسان است."`
- Units: it left ten فرنگی + six سوخاری column units `null` — `"چون ردیف‌های این دو تب مخلوط تعدادی و وزنی‌اند"` — yet wrote **zero** `field_status` entries (0/80), so the nulls carry no `unknown`/`inferred` marker.
- Disagreements: `"**هیچ فیلد مورد اختلافی (disputed) با accounts نوشته نشد**"` — QF-17 machinery unused.

Error classes it hit (errs_B6.txt, 358 lines):

| n | class |
|---|---|
| 260 | `expr identifier 'X' is not declared by inputs, outputs or a resolvable call` |
| 74 | `row 'X' member 'Y' is not a declared field` |
| 8 | `a constant (no inputs) carries expr/lang` |
| 7 | `constant output None carries no value or range` |
| 4 | `primaryKey member 'X' is not a declared field` |
| 4 | `processes[] link to 'cooking-0NN' has no process-type source naming its file` |
| 1 | `reference row 'X' is missing declared field 'Y'` |

= 4.5 errors per entry. None of these seven classes is expressible in `facts-delta.schema.json`.

## 5. The crash

Three distinct API requests, each ~10 min, each re-caching the whole ~369K-token context, each producing only an empty thinking block and no tool call:

| requestId | start | cache_creation |
|---|---|---|
| req_011Cef58aMf5tyM1rHhaWxhC | 21:47:56 | 368,681 |
| req_011Cef5thyXYpKbMpgbeBGhT | 21:58:00 | 368,743 |
| req_011Cef6ekt8359d8HakhWfVu | 22:07:52 | 368,805 |

Then at 22:17:41: `"apiError": "max_output_tokens"`, `"isApiErrorMessage": true`, text `API Error: Claude's response exceeded the 64000 output token maximum.`

**Work lost:** the entire corrected 80-entry file, three times over — nothing was written to disk between 20:53:21 and 22:30:41. ~1.1M cache-creation tokens and 38.6 min for zero bytes.

## 6. The fix rounds

**Round 1 (21:35:29)** — "fix and rewrite the same file", 358 errors, with the note `"Your error profile is identical to part B4's (the چاله‌باغ twin), class for class and count for count."` Outcome: 3.5 min diagnosis (correct), 38.6 min crash, nothing produced.

**Round 2 (22:22:18)** — the coordinator changed strategy and did the mechanical work itself: `"I already applied every mechanical fix to B6 … every `inputs[]`/`outputs[]` member's `name` is now `key` and camelCase keys are snake_case … row members `sheet_row`/`of`/`codes`/`items`/`cell`/`value` moved from `rows[]` into a sibling `data.row_meta[]` … the four unresolvable `primaryKey`s are now `[]`; and the four `process`-type source `ref`s now name the file"`. It also handed over the contract `"read from `engine/merge_facts/content.py`, not guessed"`, including the exact keyword list `if then else and or not min max sum abs round over of` and the aggregate form `sum over <input_key> of (<a> * <b>)`. It asked for a **targeted splice file** of only 64 entries. Outcome: 7.2 min, 81,623 chars, done. The agent read only 18 lines of the coordinator-modified B6.json (offset=18 limit=18) before rewriting the 64 entries.

## 7. Output-quality signals

**Counts (Write #2, the 80-entry delta):** `record` 7, `rule` 73, `item` 0, `measurement` 0, `note` 0. Rule langs: `feel` 57, `gs` 10, `const` 6. Source types cited: sheet 70, script 11, **cf 9**, process 4, validation 3. Entries carrying an actual number: **6** — T-6025=5, T-6026=140, T-6027=4, T-6028=75, T-6029=100 (grams), T-6072=0 (a colour threshold). `field_status`: 0. `confidence`: null on all 80. `scope`: identical on all 80.

Statement-level: **59/80 (74%) contain an A1-style cell/range ref**; **79/80** name a tab/column/cell/table; 17 name a `Table_*` mirror; 11 narrate the چاله‌باغ twin.

| T-6025 | «در سلول L6 تب پیتزا … تلورانس ۵ گرم … همان مقداری که در فایل گزارش شعبه چاله‌باغ هم آمده است.» | a real fact, but branch-duplicated and cell-anchored |
| T-6037 (fixed) | «… این جمع روی جدول‌های آینه فروش و نسخه اجرا می‌شود که هیچ‌کدام در این پاس تعریف نشده‌اند، بنابراین به‌جای صورت انبوهه تنها متن اصلی فرمول ثبت شده است.» + `"lang":"sheets"`, `"original":"LET(\ningredientId, 1,\namFoodIds, {71, 309, …"` | pipeline internals in the statement; raw sheet formula stored as the fact |

**Clone families** (key tail → count across the four report tabs): ruz 4, mah 4, sal 4, mojudi_avval_shab 4, daryaft_az_anbar 4, mojudi_akhar_shab 4, masraf_elami 4, masraf_vaqei 4, enheraf 4, tedad_forush 2, enheraf_ba_tolerance 2, enheraf_har_adad_ba_tolerance 2, flag_enheraf_mosbat 4, flag_enheraf_manfi 4 = **46 of 73 rules (63%)**. The dispatch then mandates the whole set be duplicated for the other branch: `"Where a rule here is byte-identical in meaning to B4's چاله‌باغ rule, it still gets its own entry"`. Store outcome: 115 `gozaresh_naharkhoran__*` + 117 `gozaresh_markazi__*` = **232 of 486 store entries (48%) are one workbook × two branches**.

## 8. Token usage

Deduplicated by `message.id` (the log splits one assistant message across several rows with repeated usage snapshots):

- **35 unique assistant messages** (73 raw rows)
- **Reported output tokens: 28,147** — a severe undercount: the streaming snapshot for the big Writes reports `output_tokens: 2`, and the three crashed requests report 0 while each exceeded 64,000. True generated output ≥ **220,000 tokens** (16,906 + 7,358 + ~65,000 + 3×~64,000 + ~51,000).
- **cache_read total: 5,107,192**
- **cache_creation total: 3,312,578**
- Peak context: `cache_creation_input_tokens` 435,861 (final turn); `cache_read_input_tokens` 381,298.
- Per-file context cost from the truncation banners: B4 59,429 · cooking-030 33,501 · formulas.tsv 30,698 · B2 28,505 · sheets.json 26,073 = **178,206 tokens** for five files, in a batch that owns 7 of 42 tabs.

## 9. Harness artifacts

`hook_additional_context` / `SubagentStart:quantify` injected **5,338 chars** at transcript indices 2, 80, 112 (once per wake): `"PONYTAIL MODE ACTIVE — level: full … You are a lazy senior developer … The best code is the code never written … Deletion over addition … Shortest working diff wins"` — a coding-persona hook fired into a Persian data-extraction agent, three times, ~1.5K tokens each.

`read_truncation_notice` attachments at indices 8, 19, 30, 49, 63 — five files truncated at a 25,000-token cap, each with an explicit paging instruction. Obeyed for 2 of 5.

summary: B7 was the cheapest and cleanest of the eight passes — and that is the problem: it is a 14-minute, ~239K-context, ~50K-output-token Opus run whose entire product is 35 "this hidden tab is a one-formula mirror of that tab" records plus 15 stubs for two workbooks it never opened. Zero items, zero measurements, zero rules, zero notes — a quantitative-facts pass that produced no quantities in structured form. All 50 landed in the store, where they are 32% of all records; store-wide, mirrors + stubs are 100 of 156 records (64%). Its own dispatch prompt already contained the answer (all 35 tab names, "each with exactly one IMPORT_FROM_SHEET-style formula", "mirror B5's structure and key shapes", the likely stub sources and where their file ids live), and I verified all 35 named-range claims byte-for-byte against names.tsv — this batch is a deterministic transcription job handed to an LLM. The dispatch prompt also ordered a documented spec violation (`foreignKeys` on mirrors, which quantify.md:87 forbids); the schema accepted it, the content validator had a hole that let it pass (its own docstring names the 84 members), and a purpose-built engine verb later deleted all 35. Its 15 stubs were scoped `warehouse`/`cashier` per quantify.md:217 and rejected by apply.py's QF-43 — a straight spec-vs-engine contradiction, "fixed" by blanking the scope to `[]`. It never opened three of its listed inputs (36 process files, the 316KB facts index, the .gs), so 0 of 50 entries carry a `processes[]` link. It ignored a truncation banner's explicit resume offset (banner said 144, it read from 168) and silently skipped 24 formula lines it then reasoned about. It never planned or outlined: one 68,899-char Write generated in a silent 389-second burst (46% of wall clock, ~78% of the 64K output cap), with no ability to validate — its toolset is Read/Glob/Write, no Bash. One factual claim ("its last row is 4 Mordad 1405") is extrapolated from a 4-row sample of a 9-row tab and propagates into a cross_record issue affecting two other batches' entries.

problems.title: The whole batch is a deterministic transcription job given to Opus
problems.evidence: Dispatch prompt (first user message, 2026-09-02 20:54:57 Tehran) enumerates all 35 tab names, asserts 'all hidden, each with exactly one IMPORT_FROM_SHEET-style formula', says 'Mirror B5's structure and key shapes', names the likely stub sources ('Anbar shobe 2.xlsx', 'Tedade Fooroosh naharkhoran.xlsx') and where their ids live. Output: all 35 data.named_range claims match names.tsv exactly (0 mismatches of 35, verified); all 35 data.import descriptors are a re-serialization of formulas.tsv rows 173-207; all 35 foreignKeys spreadsheetIds come from the SheetsFileIDs rows of rows.tsv. Cost: 14m13s, 25 tool calls, 264,531 chars of tool_result ingested, peak context 238,798 tokens.
problems.root_cause: quantify.md obligation #2 mandates 'per non-empty tab one record', and a one-formula IMPORT_FROM_SHEET tab is a non-empty tab. Nothing in the pipeline says 'a mirror tab is not a fact, it is a pointer' — so the agent is required to emit one record per mirror, which is exactly the user's complaint that mirror tables should not be recorded at all.

problems.title: Dispatch prompt ordered a documented spec violation (foreignKeys on mirrors); 35 members were later deleted by a purpose-built engine verb
problems.evidence: Dispatch prompt: '35 `role: mirror` records keyed `gozaresh_markazi__table_*` with `mirror_of` + a `foreignKeys` row'. quantify.md:87 says of an IMPORT_FROM_SHEET tab: '`mirror_of` and the rule that performs the pull — never a `foreignKeys` member, which QF-9 gives a mirror no `fields[]` to build one from.' Result: 35 of 35 B7 mirrors carry foreignKeys in the IMPORT shape {spreadsheetId, sheet, range, target}. engine/merge_facts/content.py:~372 docstring: '84 stored records carried an IMPORT descriptor here instead ... and the membership loop below read fk.get("fields") or [], so an absent fields was an empty list and every one of them passed this pass cleanly.' Store today: 0 records carry foreignKeys — removed by commits 5862498 ('a foreign key names two sides') and 4a513f5 ('a verb that removes, because the ladder never can').
problems.root_cause: The coordinator hand-wrote each batch prompt from what the previous batch did, not from the agent spec. B5 got it wrong first, the prompt canonized B5 as the template, B7 copied it. No mechanism makes a batch prompt consistent with quantify.md.

problems.title: Spec and engine contradict on stub scope — 15 validation errors, then scope erased to satisfy the validator
problems.evidence: quantify.md:217 (Record stub): 'scope the workbook's manifest row (`departments`/`branches`)'. engine/merge_facts/apply.py:334 (QF-43): 'if not set(entry["scope"]["departments"]) <= {run_dept}: out.append(f"entry {key} scoped to another department")'. B7 as written gave its 15 stubs departments ['warehouse'] (×4) and ['cashier'] (×11). Diff between the agent's Write payload and the on-disk facts-delta-B7.json is exactly 15 changes, all departments [...] -> []. Store today: 15 B7 stubs with scope.departments == [].
problems.root_cause: QF-43 was written for facts a run creates in its own department; QF-20 stubs are by definition foreign-department referents. Nobody reconciled the two, and the 'fix' was mechanical — the branch survived, the department was thrown away, so the store no longer records that Anbar shobe 2 is a warehouse artefact.

problems.title: Agent cannot validate its own output — no Bash, no Grep, one 68.9KB blind Write
problems.evidence: quantify.md frontmatter: `tools: Read, Glob, Write`. The delta is written in a single Write at 21:08:21 whose input JSON is 75,376 chars (content 68,899 chars, 50 entries). No re-read, no second Write, no self-check. It happens to be schema-clean (I ran jsonschema Draft202012 over the exact Write payload: 0 errors) but carried 15 QF-43 errors it had no way to see, since QF-43 lives in the engine's content pass, not the schema.
problems.root_cause: The agent is given the schema path and told to validate against it, but is given no tool that can run a validator. Validation is deferred to the coordinator after concatenation, so every semantic error surfaces only in the 2068-error pile.

problems.title: No plan, no outline, no incremental write — 389 silent seconds producing one monolithic Write at ~78% of the output cap
problems.evidence: Timeline: 21:01:52 assistant text 'Now I have everything. Writing the delta.' -> 21:08:21 Write (389s, 46% of the 853s run). Context jumps from 189,158 tokens (cache_read 182,743 + cache_creation 6,415 at 21:01:52) to cache_creation 238,798 at 21:09:10 — a ~49.6K-token single-message output against a 64K cap. Three earlier silent thinking gaps: 75s (20:57:46), 113s (20:59:42), 85s (21:01:52). No TodoWrite-style outline, no per-tab checkpoint, no partial file.
problems.root_cause: The agent prompt's obligation #9 is 'Write facts-delta.json' — a single terminal act. Nothing tells it to emit entries in chunks or checkpoint, so every batch is one all-or-nothing generation. This is the same shape that killed the full-mode run and the fix rounds; B7 survived only because 50 boilerplate entries happened to fit.

problems.title: Three of its listed inputs were never opened; obligations #1 and #8 not executed at all
problems.evidence: Dispatch prompt lists `process_paths: departments/cooking/processes/*.json` (36 files, 1.9 MB), `facts_index: facts/.index.json` (316,035 bytes), and 'B6 covered `Gozaresh naharkhoran.gs`; read it for orientation'. Full tool-call inventory (25 calls) shows none of the three was ever read. Result: 0 of 50 entries carry `processes[]`; the QF-34 reuse map (obligation #1: 'Load the index and the in-scope entries; build the map of keys and titles it must reuse') was never built — key reuse came only from reading B2/B5/B6 directly.
problems.root_cause: The dispatch lists inputs but sets no obligation to read them, and the agent's nine obligations are prose in a 276-line prompt with no checklist the agent must tick. Reading 2.2 MB of process files to find zero anchors also looks like waste to a cost-conscious agent, so it skips it — and the facts never attach to the process graph the system exists for.

problems.title: Ignored a truncation banner's explicit resume offset and silently lost 24 formula lines it then reasoned about
problems.evidence: Truncation attachment: '[Truncated: PARTIAL view — .../formulas.tsv: showing lines 1-143 of 208 total (30698 tokens, cap 25000). Call Read with offset=144 limit=143 for the next page, or Grep to find a specific section.' Next call (20:55:56) was Read offset=168 limit=41. Lines 144-167 = 4 سوخاری formulas (E11,F11,G11,I11) + 20 of the 25 کانتر formulas (B4..G9, including the H6:H10 deviation and J6:J10 columns). B7's T-7026 `cross_record` issue nonetheless reasons in detail about the کانتر tab's end-of-night column going to zero and 'انحراف برابر خود مصرف واقعی' — from 5 of 25 formulas.
problems.root_cause: The agent guessed a resume offset that would land it on the block it cared about (Table_* starts at line 173) instead of following the banner. Nothing in the harness detects a non-contiguous paged read. Compounding: the banner recommends Grep, which is not in this agent's toolset.

problems.title: 100% of the batch is mirrors and stubs — a quantitative-facts pass that produced zero quantitative entries
problems.evidence: Kind counts in the written delta: record 50, item 0, measurement 0, rule 0, note 0. data.role: mirror 35, log(stub) 15. data.fields[] present on 0 entries; data.rows[] on 0 entries. All 50 are in the store today (facts/records.json): 50 of 156 records = 32%. Store-wide mirrors (70, i.e. B5's 35 + B7's 35) plus stubs (30) = 100 of 156 records = 64%.
problems.root_cause: Batch design: the coordinator carved out 'the 35 Table_* mirror tabs' as a unit of work. A batch whose entire input is mirror tabs can only produce mirror records. The split guaranteed a low-value pass before the agent read a single byte.

problems.title: Every statement is spreadsheet plumbing — cells, tabs, files, named ranges in A1 notation
problems.evidence: Of 50 statements: 35 name cell A1, 35 name IMPORT_FROM_SHEET, 35 open with «تب پنهان» (hidden tab), 50 name an .xlsx file, 15 quote a named range in A1 notation (e.g. «هر سیزده ستون مبدأ (A تا M) ... زیر محدوده نام‌دار Table_Pizza_First!$A:$M می‌افتند»). Average statement 327 chars. Sample T-7028: «... ستون تاریخ آن یکپارچه («۱۴۰۴/۰۹/۱۳») است نه سه‌ستونی، و سیزده ستون آن زیر محدوده نام‌دار Table_SalesData_AmericanPizza!$A:$P می‌افتند. سه ستون آخر (کراکف #766، مخصوص #767 و مخصوص #1) در ردیف‌های نمونه‌برداری‌شده خالی‌اند.»
problems.root_cause: quantify.md tells the agent to 'cite every source with its locator' and gives a structured `source[]` + `data.location` for exactly that — but nothing tells it the `statement` must be readable without the spreadsheet. So the locator is written twice: once in structured fields, once in prose.

problems.title: One shared rule written 35 times as per-tab boilerplate
problems.evidence: The sentence fragment «در فایل Gozaresh naharkhoran.xlsx تنها یک فرمول در A1 دارد که با IMPORT_FROM_SHEET محدوده» appears verbatim in 35 of 35 mirror statements = 3,115 chars = 19% of all 16,353 statement chars. «تب داده مستقلی ندارد و آینه رکورد مبدأ است» ×15; «و ردیف‌ها اینجا تکرار نشده‌اند» ×10; «محدوده وارداتی و محدوده نام‌دار هر دو با فایل گزارش شعبه چاله‌باغ یکی است» ×5. Nine of the eleven SalesData mirrors carry the identical duplicate-date issue text.
problems.root_cause: Per-tab record emission with no generalization step. The agent is never asked 'is this the same fact you already wrote?' — exactly the tomato-line/pizza-line duplication the user complained about, in its purest form.

problems.title: Branch duplication — B5 and B7 are the same 35 records twice, and 12 of them describe the same shared source file
problems.evidence: Mean difflib similarity between B5's and B7's twin mirror statements across all 35 pairs: 0.75. The 12 Table_Ingredients_* tabs in both workbooks import from the SAME shared file Mavade Avalie.xlsx (B7 T-7042: 'محدوده A:D تب «لازانیا» فایل Mavade Avalie.xlsx'; B5 same tab: 'محدوده A:K تب «لازانیا» فایل Mavade Avalie.xlsx'), so 24 store records describe 12 source tabs, once per branch. Both mirror_of the same 12 B3 records T-3088..T-3099.
problems.root_cause: The pipeline records the mirror, not the source. Two branches importing the same recipe file therefore produce two records per recipe tab — the same defect as 'notes duplicated per branch', originating in the mirror-record rule rather than in note handling.

problems.title: A factual claim extrapolated from a 4-row sample, propagated as a cross_record issue affecting two other batches
problems.evidence: T-7026 issue: «محدوده پرشده این آینه A1:Q9 است، یعنی تنها هشت ردیف داده دارد و آخرین ردیفش ۴ مرداد ۱۴۰۵ است ... GET_ROW_BY_PERSIAN_DATE روی این جدول ردیفی پیدا نمی‌کند و ستون موجودی آخر شب تب «کانتر» صفر می‌شود؛ در نتیجه مصرف اعلامی صفر و انحراف برابر خود مصرف واقعی درمی‌آید.» sheets.json for Table_KitchenCounter_Last: rows=9, dimension A1:Q9, and `head` contains exactly 4 data rows (days 1,2,3,4). Rows 5-8 exist and were never dumped. The 8-row count is correct; 'last row is 4 Mordad' is the sample's last row, not the tab's. issues[].affects lists T-7026, T-2011 (B2) and T-6006 (B6).
problems.root_cause: sheets.json exposes `rows` (true count) and `head` (5-row sample) with no marker that `head` is a sample; the agent read the last visible row as the last row. No confidence marker or field_status was attached to the inference, and no tool existed to check it.

problems.title: Stubs assert the structure of files the same sentence admits were never read
problems.evidence: 15 stub statements, e.g. T-7001: «تب «پیتزا» در فایل Anbar shobe 2.xlsx: به ازای هر شب یک ردیف با تاریخ شمسی تفکیک‌شده (روز، ماه، سال) و مقدار تحویل‌شده هر قلم لاین پیتزا از انبار شعبه دو. ... خود فایل در این پاس خوانده نشده و ساختار ستون‌هایش اینجا ثبت نشده است.» The two source dumps existed on disk — the agent globbed 1Te8IMhl…/* at 20:59:46 and read only its 310-byte meta.json, same for 10Jsuk…. field_status marks only `data/role` as inferred; the asserted grain and column semantics carry no marker.
problems.root_cause: The dispatch scoped the batch to one workbook, so the agent opened the source dumps' meta.json only to get file ids, then described their content from the mirror's headers. QF-20 stubs are meant to be empty placeholders; nothing stops an agent filling one with inference.

problems.title: Batch-run vocabulary leaked into permanent store text
problems.evidence: «در این پاس» ('in this pass') appears in 15 of B7's 50 statements and in 30 records of the current store. The store is permanent; 'this pass' refers to a batch that existed for 14 minutes on 2026-09-02.
problems.root_cause: The agent was told it is 'batch 7 of 8' and wrote its situational awareness into the fact text. Nothing in quantify.md forbids process/run vocabulary in a `statement`.

problems.title: Excel cosmetics and sampling artefacts recorded as issues
problems.evidence: 24 issues total, kinds: junk 13, column_shift 7, scale 1, unit_kind 1, cross_record 1, bug 1. Examples of `junk`: T-7021 «عنوان ستون M در این آینه رشته «Column 1» است و همه سلول‌های آن خالی‌اند»; T-7028 «سه ستون آخر (کراکف #766، مخصوص #767 و مخصوص #1) در ردیف‌های نمونه‌برداری‌شده خالی‌اند» (empty only in the 4-row sample); T-7021 statement «یک ستون سیزدهم بی‌عنوان و خالی هم به دنبال آن‌ها می‌آید». `column_shift` ×7 records a named range stopping one column short.
problems.root_cause: 'Note every data issue' with no value threshold. 20 of 24 issues are spreadsheet hygiene, not restaurant facts; only the `scale` (grams vs units, F7 = 0.002) and the duplicate-date `bug` are operationally meaningful.

problems.title: Cross-branch comparison prose in 15 statements — facts about two spreadsheets, not about the restaurant
problems.evidence: 15 of 50 statements compare to the چاله‌باغ twin, e.g. T-7025: «برخلاف تب هم‌نام گزارش شعبه چاله‌باغ اینجا ستون خالی ابتدایی وجود ندارد، پس ستون‌ها جابه‌جا نشده‌اند و موجودی اول شب لیموناد خوشگوار ##757 به فرمول‌های تب «کانتر» می‌رسد.» Ordered by the dispatch: 'where this workbook's ingredient table differs from the چاله‌باغ twin's ... say so.'
problems.root_cause: The dispatch asked for a diff against B5 in the return summary; the agent put the diff inside every statement as well. A per-run diff is a review artefact, not a durable fact.

problems.title: The 84 malformed foreignKeys members passed the content validator cleanly
problems.evidence: engine/merge_facts/content.py `_check_record_shape` docstring: 'both halves are required ... 84 stored records carried an IMPORT descriptor here instead (`{spreadsheetId, sheet, range, target}`), and the membership loop below read `fk.get("fields") or []`, so an absent `fields` was an empty list and every one of them passed this pass cleanly.' Also verified: facts-delta.schema.json has no `foreignKeys` definition at all (grep: no match), so the schema constrains nothing there.
problems.root_cause: `fk.get("fields") or []` treats an absent required key as an empty collection instead of an error — a null-coalescing bug that turned a required-field check into a no-op. Fixed only after 84 bad members reached the store.

problems.title: Schema-clean but semantically wrong — the only gate the agent can reach checks almost nothing
problems.evidence: The exact Write payload validates against facts-delta.schema.json with 0 errors (jsonschema Draft202012Validator). Its 15 real errors (QF-43) and its 35 malformed foreignKeys are invisible to that schema. The schema's `entry` def is one `allOf` requiring only {kind,key,title,statement,scope,source,retired,data} plus 2-3 keys inside `data` per kind.
problems.root_cause: The data contract is frozen and deliberately permissive (`data` is largely free-form); all real checking lives in the engine's content pass, which the agent has no tool to invoke. The agent is told to 'validate against facts-delta.schema.json' — advice that would have passed anyway.

problems.title: Wasted round trip on a path built by concatenating an absolute data_root with a relative run_dir
problems.evidence: 20:55:08 Read '/home/lili/.../process dev/runs/facts/cooking/20260902-080737/parts/facts-delta-B5.json' -> error: 'File does not exist. Note: your current working directory is /home/lili/.../process dev/data-repo. Did you mean .../data-repo/runs/facts/...'. The dispatch gives `run_dir: runs/facts/cooking/20260902-080737/` (relative) next to `data_root: /home/.../data-repo` (absolute).
problems.root_cause: The dispatch header mixes relative and absolute path conventions in adjacent lines with no statement of which root the relative ones hang off.

problems.title: The 25K-token read cap forced 5 extra paged calls and is where the only content loss happened
problems.evidence: Three truncation notices: facts-delta-B5.json (lines 1-60 of 107, 37,756 tokens), sheets.json (lines 1-2710 of 3,326, 26,073 tokens), formulas.tsv (lines 1-143 of 208, 30,698 tokens). Of 21 Read calls, 12 carried offset/limit and 10 were re-entries into an already-opened file. sheets.json and B5 were reassembled correctly; formulas.tsv was not (lines 144-167 lost).
problems.root_cause: Paging a structured dump by line number puts the burden of contiguity on the model. A dump-side per-tab or per-sheet read (or a `dump-workbook --tabs Table_*` slice) would have handed this batch ~35 tiny files instead of a 208-line TSV to page.

problems.title: Interleaved thinking is stored empty — the three long silent gaps are unrecoverable
problems.evidence: 15 thinking blocks in the transcript, every one `{"type":"thinking","thinking":"","signature":"CAIS..."}`. The gaps at 20:57:46 (75s), 20:59:42 (113s) and 21:01:52 (85s) contain no readable reasoning, so why it chose offset=168 over the banner's 144, and how it decided the 12 ingredient mirrors were value-identical to B3's records without reading B3, cannot be recovered.
problems.root_cause: Encrypted thinking persisted with signature only. Forensics on these runs is limited to tool calls and final text.

problems.title: Token accounting in the transcript is unusable for cost or limit monitoring
problems.evidence: The 21:08:21 message whose tool_use block is 75,376 chars reports `output_tokens: 2`. Across the 20 unique assistant messages, last-record output_tokens sums to 3,528 — off by more than an order of magnitude. Real output is only inferable from the cache_creation jump (189,158 -> 238,798 = ~49.6K tokens for the Write). Total cache_read across the 20 messages: 2,020,012.
problems.root_cause: Per-streaming-chunk usage records carry the request header's usage, not the completed message's. Any monitor that would have caught 'this turn is at 78% of the output cap' before the crash-prone batches ran cannot be built from this data.

problems.title: Two identical mirror batches (B5, B7) run sequentially inside a ~3-hour chain
problems.evidence: Subagent windows: B5 'Quantify batch 5 central mirror tables' 16:31:57 -> 16:44:59 (13 min), B7 'Quantify batch 7 naharkhoran mirror tables' 17:24:57 -> 17:39:10 (14 min), B8 started 17:39:40. B5 and B7 do the same job on twin workbooks; B7's only dependency on B5 is 'mirror B5's structure and key shapes'. B5 and B7 are also the only two of the eight whose transcripts end at completion — every other batch (B1,B2,B3,B4,B6,B8) has events hours later, i.e. fix rounds.
problems.root_cause: The coordinator serialized all eight passes to keep the shared temp-id space and 'never re-propose an earlier part's entry' rule safe. The two mechanical batches added ~27 minutes to the critical path and contributed 100 low-value store entries, while the batches that needed help were the semantic ones.

problems.title: Cross-part temp-id references work only because a sibling part happened to contain them
problems.evidence: B7 emits 12 refs T-3088..T-3099 (B3's mavade_avalie__* records) and all 12 resolve correctly — but facts-delta-B3.json was never read (25-call inventory). The ids came from B5's mirror_of fields, which B7 did read. Likewise T-2006..T-2013 were confirmed by partial reads of B2 (5 calls, lines 1-2, 3-32, 150-399, 200, 412-541 — lines 33-149 and 400-411 never read).
problems.root_cause: A 7000-block temp-id convention with no id manifest. Correctness of every cross-part ref depends on each agent finding the id somewhere in whichever earlier parts it chose to open. B7 got lucky; nothing structural made it safe.

problems.title: No confidence or inference marking on 22 claims that rest on samples and inference
problems.evidence: field_status appears on 15 of 50 entries and always with the same single value `{"data/role": "inferred"}` (the stubs). The 4-row-sample claim in T-7026, the 10 'مقادیر سلول‌به‌سلول با رکورد مرجع مبدأ یکی‌اند' claims made without opening B3 or the Mavade Avalie dump, and the 15 stubs' asserted grain all carry no marker. 0 entries use `accounts[]`, 0 use `valid_from`.
problems.root_cause: QF-6 defines field_status per-field, and the agent applied it only where the dispatch prompt reminded it to (stubs). Nothing derives 'this came from a 5-row head sample' automatically, and the agent has no way to tell a full dump from a sampled one.

## 0. Files

## 3. How it built the delta

No plan, no outline, no todo list, no incremental writes. One assistant sentence ("Now I have everything. Writing the delta.") then a single `Write` of 68,899 chars / 50 entries after 389 seconds. Never re-read the file it wrote. Could **not** self-check: `tools: Read, Glob, Write` (quantify.md frontmatter) — no Bash, no Grep, so no `merge facts check`, no `python -c json.load`, not even a line count. It did produce syntactically valid JSON on the first attempt, and the payload validates schema-clean (jsonschema Draft202012Validator: 0 errors).

## 4. What it got wrong / could not know

Reasoning is unrecoverable — all 15 `thinking` blocks are `{"thinking": "", "signature": "CAIS…"}`. What is visible:

- **Ignored the resume offset it was given.** Banner: *"showing lines 1-143 of 208 total (30698 tokens, cap 25000). Call Read with offset=144 limit=143 for the next page, or Grep to find a specific section."* Next call: `offset=168 limit=41`. Lines 144-167 = سوخاری E11/F11/G11/I11 + کانتر B4..G9 (20 of 25). It read only کانتر I9, E10, F10, G10, I10 — yet T-7026's issue reasons about the کانتر consumption/deviation columns.
- **The banner recommends Grep, which this agent does not have.**
- **Sampled `head` read as complete data.** `sheets.json` gives `rows: 9` and a 4-data-row `head` for `Table_KitchenCounter_Last`; the agent wrote «آخرین ردیفش ۴ مرداد ۱۴۰۵ است» as fact.
- **Asserted equality with records it never opened.** 10 ingredient mirrors say «مقادیر سلول‌به‌سلول با رکورد مرجع مبدأ یکی‌اند»; B3 (the source records) was never read.
- **Cross-part refs were lifted from B5, not verified.** All 12 `T-3088..T-3099` refs are correct — I checked them against B3 on disk — but they were copied out of B5's `mirror_of` fields.
- **What it got right, mechanically:** 35/35 `data.named_range` claims match `names.tsv` byte-for-byte; all `foreignKeys` spreadsheetIds match the `SheetsFileIDs` rows of `rows.tsv`; the duplicate-date finding is real (9 of 11 SalesData tabs show `1404/09/14` twice in `head`; AmericanPizza and SinglePizza do not); the scale finding is real (`Table_Pizza_Request` head 13 آذر: rost beef 5000, ham 6000, chicken 8000, while formulas.tsv `پیتزا F7` cached = `0.002`).

## 5. Crash

**None.** The run completed in one turn. But the single Write consumed ~49.6K output tokens (context 189,158 → 238,798) against the 64K cap — **~78% of the ceiling for 50 boilerplate entries.** Any batch with real content at this entry count dies, which is what happened elsewhere.

## 6. Fix message

**None reached this agent** — the transcript's last event is 17:39:10Z, 49 s after the Write. The fix was applied externally: the only diff between the agent's payload and the on-disk `facts-delta-B7.json` is 15 changes, all `"departments": ["warehouse"|"cashier"]` → `"departments": []` (plus a full pretty-print reformat at Sep 3 01:22).
